lessons.title: Fillers that buy time: ну, вот, значит, короче, типа and как бы, and the register each one signals
lessons.explanation: A filler is a word that holds the floor while the speaker assembles the next clause, and Russian has a small set of them that recur so often that a learner who cannot hear them separately hears only noise. The Russian term is слова-паразиты (SLO-va pa-ra-ZEE-ty), literally 'parasite words', and it is a prescriptive label rather than a neutral one: the Russian Wikipedia article under that title collects the ordinary list, ну, вот, значит, короче, типа, как бы, and treats them as weeds in speech. That framing is worth knowing because it explains how Russian speakers themselves judge these words, and it is also the reason a learner should not treat the list as six synonyms. Each one does a different job, and each one has a different tolerance for writing. Start with ну (NOO), 'well'. The Russian Wiktionary gives it two headings, one as междометие (meezh-da-MYE-tee-ye), 'interjection', and one as частица (chas-TEE-tsa), 'particle', which is the grammatical trace of its double life. As an interjection it is a hesitation sound, the Russian counterpart of a drawn-out 'well'. As a particle it softens or urges: «Ну, не знаю» (NOO, ne ZNA-yoo), 'well, I don't know', takes the edge off a doubt, while «Ну давай!» (NOO da-VAY), 'come on then!', pushes. Intonation separates them: a long falling ну opens a hesitation, a short rising ну urges. вот (VOT), 'here, this, that is', is a pointing word. It directs attention to something present or just said, and it is the backbone of a family of set phrases: «вот и всё» (VOT ee VSYO), 'that's it, that's all', «вот это да» (VOT EH-ta DA), 'wow', «вот в чём дело» (VOT f chyom DYE-la), 'that's what it is about'. Unlike the others, вот survives in written Russian as a demonstrative, which is why it is the least stigmatised item on the list. значит (ZNA-cheet), 'so, then, that means', is the third person singular of значить (ZNA-cheet), 'to mean', and it works as an inference marker: it announces that what follows is a consequence or a summary of what came before. «Значит, ты не придёшь» (ZNA-cheet, ty ne pree-DYOSH), 'so you are not coming', is a conclusion, not a filler, and the same word becomes a filler when it merely announces that the speaker is about to organise an answer, as in «Значит, так» (ZNA-cheet, TAK), 'right, then'. короче (KO-ro-che) is the comparative of короткий (ka-ROT-keey), 'short', and as a вводное слово (vva-DNO-ye SLO-va), 'parenthetical word', it means 'to cut it short, in short'. It is the most dangerous item on the list: it tells the hearer that detail is being dropped and, by implication, that the speaker wants to get to the end. Among friends that is efficient; in a meeting it sounds impatient, and to an older listener it can sound dismissive. типа (TEE-pa) is the genitive of тип (TEEP), 'type', used as a particle meaning 'sort of, like', and the Russian Wiktionary labels it разговорное (raz-ga-VOR-na-ye), 'colloquial', with the synonyms вроде (VRO-dee) and как бы (kak BY). It is strongly youth-marked and strongly criticised, which is exactly why it is useful to recognise and risky to produce. как бы (kak BY), 'as if, sort of', contains the conditional particle бы (BY) that lesson 104 treated in its grammatical role; here the same particle marks distance from the accuracy of what is being said. «Он как бы директор» (on kak BY dee-RYEK-tar), 'he is sort of the director', hedges the claim and can also hint that he is not really. The five items form a rough ladder of acceptability in writing. вот and значит are at home in expository prose, where they point and infer. ну appears in written dialogue and in messages, rarely in reports. короче and типа belong to speech and to messaging, and как бы sits with them but has a formal written use in the construction 'as if', where it is not a filler at all. A learner's practical rule is to recognise all six, produce ну, вот and значит freely, produce короче only among peers, and avoid типа and filler как бы until the surrounding register is secure.
lessons.example: One turn, then the same content without fillers. «Ну, значит, короче, я опоздал, потому что автобус, типа, не пришёл». (NOO, ZNA-cheet, KO-ro-che, ya a-paz-DAL, pa-ta-MOO shto af-TO-boos, TEE-pa, ne pree-SHOL.) 'Well, so, in short, I was late because the bus, like, did not come.' The sentence is understandable and it is also a caricature: three openers before the content, one of them the impatient короче, and типа hedging a fact that needs no hedge. Now the same content organised. «Я опоздал: автобус не пришёл». (ya a-paz-DAL: af-TO-boos ne pree-SHOL.) 'I was late: the bus did not come.' Nothing has been lost except the performance of thinking aloud. A second version shows how one marker can do real work. «Ну, автобус не пришёл, вот я и опоздал». (NOO, af-TO-boos ne pree-SHOL, VOT ya ee a-paz-DAL.) 'Well, the bus did not come, and that is why I was late.' Here ну opens the explanation without claiming precision, and вот я и (VOT ya ee) marks the consequence as following from the fact just given, which is the demonstrative use of вот rather than filler. A third version moves the same story into writing. «Опоздал: автобус не пришёл. Извините за задержку». (a-paz-DAL: af-TO-boos ne pree-SHOL. eez-vee-NEE-tye za za-DYERZH-koo.) 'I was late: the bus did not come. Sorry for the delay.' The written version keeps the colon, because the colon is the written equivalent of значит: it announces that an explanation follows. That substitution, a punctuation mark for a spoken marker, is the single most useful transfer in this lesson.
lessons.question: You are drafting a short written report and you write «Ну, короче, мы почти закончили». A colleague marks it. What is wrong, and what are the two repairs, one formal and one slightly less formal?
lessons.answer: Both markers are spoken: ну opens a turn in conversation, and короче (KO-ro-che) announces compression with an impatient edge, so in a report the sentence reads as a transcript; the repairs are «Работа почти закончена» (ra-BO-ta POCH-tee za-KON-che-na), 'the work is almost finished', for the formal register, and «Почти закончили» (pa-CHTEE za-KON-chee-lee), 'we have almost finished', for a neutral internal note.
lessons.distractor: Nothing is wrong, because ну and короче are neutral connectors and the only issue is the missing comma after короче.
lessons.correction: The comma is not the problem, and adding one would make the sentence tidier without making it written. The register is the problem. ну is a turn-opening particle: it presupposes a hearer and a moment of hesitation, neither of which a report has. короче is worse, because its meaning is 'to cut it short', and a report that announces compression implies that the writer has been keeping the reader waiting. The repair is not a synonym swap but a change of construction: a passive or impersonal clause states the result and drops the speaker altogether, which is the same move lesson 82 described as the written end of the register ladder. If you need to keep a first person plural, «Почти закончили» is acceptable in an internal note because internal notes tolerate a spoken colour; a report does not.

depth.definitions: A filler is a word or sound that occupies a turn while the speaker plans, without adding propositional content. A discourse marker is a word that organises the relation between what is being said and what came before, and some fillers double as markers. A частица (chas-TEE-tsa), 'particle', is an uninflected word expressing the speaker's stance or organising the utterance, and it is the class that ну, вот and типа belong to in dictionaries. A вводное слово (vva-DNO-ye SLO-va), 'parenthetical word', is a word that comments on the utterance rather than forming part of it, which is why короче is set off by commas. A междометие (meezh-da-MYE-tee-ye), 'interjection', is an isolable emotional or interactional sound, the heading under which the Russian Wiktionary lists ну in its first section. Register here means the social calibration of the word: who may say it to whom, in which channel. Prerequisites: the particles of lesson 102 supply the stance vocabulary, and lesson 82 supplies the written and spoken split this lesson applies word by word.
depth.mechanism: The mechanism behind all six is floor-holding. Conversation runs at a speed that thought does not, so a speaker who needs a fraction of a second has three options: stop and yield the turn, produce a sound, or produce a word that means 'I am still here and the next part is coming'. Russian prefers the third, and the specific word chosen tells the hearer what kind of continuation to expect. ну says 'I am starting, and I may be conceding'. вот says 'look at this, the next item is the point'. значит says 'I am drawing a conclusion'. короче says 'I am skipping to the end'. типа and как бы say 'do not hold me to the exact wording'. That is why they are not interchangeable: each one is a promise about the shape of what follows. The promise is also why they are stigmatised. A speaker who says короче and then talks for two minutes has broken the promise, and the hearer registers the word as noise. The prescriptive literature on слова-паразиты is essentially a catalogue of broken promises, which is why the same words are described both as indispensable and as parasites.
depth.secondExample: Here is the same set in a service encounter, where the choice of filler is a choice about politeness. A customer telephones a clinic. «Алло, здравствуйте. Ну, вот, я записывался на четверг, но, значит, планы изменились». (al-LO, zdra-stvooy-tye. NOO, VOT, ya za-PEE-sy-val-sya na cheet-VYERK, no, ZNA-cheet, PLA-ny eez-mee-NEE-lees.) 'Hello. Well, you see, I had an appointment for Thursday, but, so, my plans changed.' «Конечно. Давайте перенесём». (ka-NYESH-na. da-VAY-tye pee-ree-nee-SYOM.) 'Of course. Let us move it.' «Спасибо. Короче, мне удобнее в пятницу». (spa-SEE-ba. KO-ro-che, mnye oo-DOB-nee-ye f PYA-tee-tsoo.) 'Thank you. In short, Friday suits me better.' The first speaker uses ну and вот to soften the opening and значит to flag that a consequence is coming, all three of them doing social work: they make the change of plans sound like a narrative rather than a demand. The same speaker then uses короче to the receptionist, and the effect is a slight drop in formality at the exact moment when the request is made. It is not rude, because the request is small and the thanks has already been given, but a learner should notice that the register moved. With an older receptionist or in a letter, «Мне удобнее в пятницу» (mnye oo-DOB-nee-ye f PYA-tee-tsoo), 'Friday suits me better', does the same work with no marker at all.
depth.mistake: Four errors recur. The first is treating the six as synonyms for 'well' and using them at random, which produces the caricature in the example. Diagnostic: count the markers in a thirty-second turn; more than one opener per turn is a signal that you are performing hesitation rather than thinking. The second is importing короче into writing because it feels efficient. Diagnostic: if the text has no addressee who can interrupt, короче has nothing to do. The third is using типа and как бы as hedges for facts that are certain, as in «я типа опоздал» (ya TEE-pa a-paz-DAL), 'I was sort of late', which sounds evasive or teenage depending on the hearer. Diagnostic: ask whether you would accept the same hedge in your own language; if not, delete it. The fourth is a comprehension error rather than a production error: hearing значит as a filler when it is an inference, and therefore missing the conclusion. «Значит, ты не придёшь» is not 'so, you are not coming' in the sense of a casual opener; it is an inference from something the other person has just said, and the reply «Почему?» (pa-chee-MOO), 'why?', shows that the inference was heard. A related transfer error affects speakers of English, who use 'like' as a filler and map it onto типа; the mapping is close in function and much narrower in acceptable company, because типа is marked as youth speech in a way that 'like' no longer is.
depth.application: Record yourself, or write out, a ninety-second account of something that went wrong yesterday, in Russian, using no fillers at all. Then rewrite it with exactly three markers, choosing one opener, one inference and one hedge, and no more. Read both versions aloud and mark where you wanted to insert a fourth. Those points are where your Russian is still searching for a construction, and the construction, not the filler, is the thing to learn. Next, take a message you have actually sent in Russian and underline every item from this lesson. For each one write in English what promise it made about the continuation. Delete the ones whose promise the sentence did not keep. Finally, write the same content as a three-line formal note and replace each deleted marker with a punctuation mark or an explicit connective, a colon for значит, «таким образом» (ta-KEEM OB-ra-zom), 'thus', for an inference, and nothing at all for ну. The exercise takes about twenty-five minutes and leaves you with a personal list of the markers you overuse.
depth.summary: The six fillers are six different promises, not six ways of saying 'well'. ну opens and softens, вот points, значит infers, короче compresses and hurries, типа and как бы hedge the accuracy of the wording. Dictionaries split ну between interjection and particle and mark типа as colloquial, which is the lexicographic trace of how Russian speakers judge them. All six are at home in speech and in messaging; вот and значит also belong to expository prose, ну to written dialogue, and короче and типа to the spoken end of the ladder. The practical skill is two-sided: hear which promise is being made so that you do not miss an inference, and produce only the markers whose promise you intend to keep. When in doubt in writing, replace the marker with punctuation or with an explicit connective, because a colon can do everything значит does and never sounds like a transcript.

readings.title: Википедия, «Слова-паразиты»
readings.note: Read the lead and the list of examples. The article gives the Russian term for fillers, explains that they carry no propositional meaning and that they are judged as a speech defect, and lists ну, вот, значит, короче, типа and как бы among the usual suspects. It is the source for the prescriptive framing this lesson pushes back against. Caveat: it is a popular encyclopaedia article with thin sourcing and a strongly purist tone, so use it for the vocabulary and the social attitude, not for grammatical analysis.

readings.title: Wikipedia, 'Filler (linguistics)'

The article supplies the general model used here, that a filler occupies a turn while planning continues and that some fillers also organise discourse, which is why the same word can be both noise and signal. visual.title: Filler grid: six markers against three jobs and three registers
visual.description: A labelled text grid with the six fillers down the left, three columns for the discourse job they do and three rows for the registers in which they are acceptable. Rendered as text steps rather than as an image.
steps: Step 1, draw the grid. Six rows labelled ну, вот, значит, короче, типа, как бы. Three columns headed 'opens or softens', 'points or infers', 'compresses or hedges'.

Step 2, mark the jobs. Put an X in the cell each marker actually performs, and write the promise beside it in English: ну 'I am starting and may concede', вот 'look at this', значит 'therefore', короче 'skipping ahead', типа and как бы 'do not hold me to the wording'. Leave the other cells empty; the empty cells are the point.

Step 3, add the register rows. Under the grid draw three bands labelled 'report or article', 'letter or internal note', 'message or speech'. Write each filler into the lowest band where it is comfortable, and draw an arrow upwards only where the marker also has a non-filler written use, which applies to вот and значит.

Step 4, add the substitution table. In a fourth band write the written equivalent for each marker: a colon for значит, «таким образом» (ta-KEEM OB-ra-zom) for an inference, nothing for ну, and a deleted clause for короче, because the written fix for compression is to cut the text rather than to announce the cut.

Step 5, test one sentence. Take «Ну, короче, мы почти закончили» and move it through the three bands, writing the version that belongs in each. The exercise is complete when the top-band version contains no marker at all.

lessons.title: The listener's toolbar: да ладно, серьёзно, вот это да, ничего себе, класс, ужас and ой
lessons.explanation: A conversation is not built from turns alone. Between the turns there is a layer of short reactions that tells the speaker how the last thing landed, and Russian has a compact set of them that a learner needs both to produce and, more urgently, to read correctly. The grammatical category is междометие (meezh-da-MYE-tee-ye), 'interjection', an uninflected word that stands outside the clause and expresses a reaction rather than a proposition. Two of the seven in this lesson are nouns doing interjection work without changing shape: класс (KLAS), 'class', used as 'cool', and ужас (OO-zhas), 'horror', used as 'awful'. That zero-derivation is worth noticing because it explains the register: a noun pressed into service as a reaction keeps the flavour of the noun, which is why класс sounds like school or student speech and ужас sounds like genuine distress. Start with the pair that causes the most misunderstanding. «Да ладно!» (da LAD-na), literally 'oh, come on', is disbelief, the Russian 'no way', and it can also be dismissal, the Russian 'never mind, forget it'. The two readings are told apart by what precedes. After a piece of news it is disbelief and it invites confirmation, so the natural follow-up from the speaker is «Правда» (PRAV-da), 'really', or a repetition of the fact. After an apology or an offer of help it is dismissal, and the natural follow-up is a change of subject. серьёзно (see-RYOZ-na), 'seriously', is the adverb of серьёзный (see-RYOZ-ny), 'serious', and as a reaction it questions whether the speaker means it. A rising «Серьёзно?» (see-RYOZ-na) is sceptical; a flat «Серьёзно» with a nod is acceptance of something surprising. «Вот это да» (VOT EH-ta DA), 'that is something', is unambiguous admiration, and it is the safest of the positive reactions because it cannot be heard as envy. «Ничего себе» (nee-chee-VO see-BYEH), literally 'nothing to myself', is the widest of them: admiration, astonishment, or indignation, with the reading carried by tone and context. Said about a price it is usually indignation, said about a view from a window it is admiration. It is informal but not slangy, and it is usable with people you address as вы. класс (KLAS) is the peer-to-peer positive reaction, roughly 'cool', and it is marked as youth speech; said to a professor about her research it is too casual, and said about a restaurant it is perfectly ordinary. ужас (OO-zhas) is the negative counterpart, 'awful, terrible', and it is strong: it evaluates the thing, not the person, but it leaves little room for disagreement. ой (OY) is the softest item, 'oh', and it has a second career as a pre-apology, «Ой, извините» (OY, eez-vee-NEE-tye), 'oh, sorry', which softens the interruption before it happens. The toolbar is not a list of synonyms for 'wow'. Each button commits the listener to an evaluation, and the evaluations differ in direction and in strength. For a learner the practical priorities are, first, to hear «да ладно» correctly, because misreading dismissal as disbelief produces the wrong reply; second, to avoid ужас when you mean admiration, because it is the error with the highest social cost; and third, to keep класс for peers. A last point about placement: these words occupy the slot before the substantive reply, and Russian tolerates two of them in a row, «Ой, ничего себе» (OY, nee-chee-VO see-BYEH), 'oh, wow', but rarely three. When they cluster, the speaker is stalling, and the same criticism that applies to fillers applies here.
lessons.example: Four exchanges with the same news and four different reactions. News: «Я переезжаю в Лиссабон». (ya pee-ree-ye-ZHA-yoo f lee-sa-BON.) 'I am moving to Lisbon.' First, disbelief: «Да ладно! Когда?» (da LAD-na! kag-DA?) 'No way! When?' Second, astonishment that commits to nothing yet: «Ничего себе. А работа?» (nee-chee-VO see-BYEH. a ra-BO-ta?) 'Wow. And work?' Third, admiration: «Вот это да! Молодец». (VOT EH-ta DA! ma-la-DYETS.) 'That is something! Well done.' Fourth, the error: «Ужас!» (OO-zhas) 'Awful!', which reads as a judgement on the move and requires an immediate repair, «Ой, это не то слово! Это здорово». (OY, EH-ta ne to SLO-va! EH-ta ZDA-ro-va.) 'Oh, that is the wrong word! It is great.' The four reactions are not interchangeable, and the fourth shows why: ужас evaluates the decision as bad, so the speaker hears that you think she is making a mistake. A fifth exchange shows the dismissal sense of the same phrase that opened the set. «Извини, я забыл твою книгу». (eez-vee-NEE, ya za-BYL tva-YOO KNEE-goo.) 'Sorry, I forgot your book.' «Да ладно, потом отдашь». (da LAD-na, pa-TOM at-DASH.) 'Never mind, give it to me later.' No exclamation mark, no rising tone, and the phrase is now a release rather than a challenge. Compare the punctuation and the intonation in the two uses: disbelief is high and short, dismissal is low and level, and the difference is entirely prosodic, which is why a written «да ладно» needs context to be read at all.
lessons.question: A colleague shows you photos of her new flat and you say «Ужас!» meaning that you are overwhelmed. She goes quiet. What did she hear, and what should you have said?
lessons.answer: She heard a negative evaluation of the flat, because ужас (OO-zhas) means 'horror, awful' and commits the speaker to a bad judgement; the admiration reactions are «Вот это да» (VOT EH-ta DA) or «Ничего себе» (nee-chee-VO see-BYEH), and «Ой, как здорово» (OY, kak ZDA-ro-va), 'oh, how lovely', is the warmest repair.
lessons.distractor: She heard admiration, because ужас is the standard Russian reaction to something impressive.
lessons.correction: ужас is a noun meaning 'horror' and its reaction use keeps the negative direction; it never means 'wow'. What happened is a transfer from English, where 'that's insane' and 'crazy' have flipped to mean 'impressive' in colloquial use. Russian has not made that flip with ужас, and the word still reports distress, so the colleague heard a verdict on her flat. The repair is not a softer ужас but a positive item from the same toolbar, and «Ой, как здорово» adds the ой that signals the reaction was spontaneous. Note that «ничего себе» can be positive or negative depending on tone, which makes it a poor choice for a repair; «вот это да» has only the admiring reading, which is why it is the safe one.

depth.definitions: An interjection is an uninflected word that expresses a reaction and stands outside the clause. A backchannel is a short listener response that signals attention without claiming the turn, and several items here work as backchannels as well as reactions. Evaluation is the direction and strength of the judgement a reaction carries: вот это да is positive and strong, класс is positive and casual, ничего себе is bidirectional, ужас is negative and strong, ой is neutral and weak. A pre-apology is a word placed before an imposition to soften it, which is ой in «Ой, извините». Zero-derivation is the use of a word from one class in another without a change of form, which is how класс and ужас became interjections. Prerequisites: the particles of lesson 102 for stance, and the fillers of lesson 141, since reactions and fillers share the pre-turn slot and differ in what they commit the speaker to.
depth.mechanism: The mechanism is evaluation at the point of receipt. A speaker offers a piece of news, and the listener's first word decides whether the news has been accepted, questioned or rejected before any content is discussed. Russian reactions are efficient because each one bundles a direction with a strength. «Да ладно» bundles disbelief with an invitation to confirm, so it keeps the conversation open. «Серьёзно?» bundles scepticism with a request for evidence. «Вот это да» bundles admiration with no request at all, which closes the evaluation happily. «Ничего себе» bundles high arousal with no fixed direction, which is why it needs tone to complete it. класс bundles approval with a peer relationship, and that is why it misfires upwards. ужас bundles condemnation with high strength, which is why it misfires when the speaker expected congratulation. Understanding the bundle explains the social effects without any need for a list of translations: the word does not mean a feeling, it performs an evaluation and thereby assigns a relationship.
depth.secondExample: A workplace exchange shows how the toolbar sets the tone of a whole conversation. «Ты слышал, проект закрыли?» (ty SLY-shal, pra-YEKT za-KREE-lee?) 'Did you hear, the project has been closed?' «Да ладно. Совсем?» (da LAD-na. saf-SYEM?) 'No way. Completely?' «Совсем. Всё, никого не осталось». (saf-SYEM. VSYO, nee-ka-VO ne a-STA-las.) 'Completely. That's it, nobody is left.' «Ужас. А люди что?» (OO-zhas. a LYOO-dee shto?) 'That's awful. And what about the people?' «Ничего себе, ты первый, кто спросил». (nee-chee-VO see-BYEH, ty PYER-vy, kto spra-SEEL.) 'Wow, you are the first person to ask.' Four observations. The first reaction is disbelief, and the follow-up «Совсем?» (saf-SYEM), 'completely?', shows that «да ладно» was heard as an invitation to confirm rather than as a comment on the news. The second is ужас, which is appropriate here because the news is bad and the evaluation aligns with the speaker's. The third is «ничего себе» in its astonished sense, and the tone makes it admiring rather than indignant, which is the bidirectional problem in action. Throughout, the reactions come first and the questions second, which is the normal order: evaluate, then ask. A learner who inverts it, asking the question first and the reaction never, sounds like someone taking a survey.
depth.mistake: Three errors dominate. The first is using ужас for admiration, usually under the influence of English slang in which 'insane' and 'crazy' became positive. Diagnostic: ask whether the word's noun meaning is compatible with the thing being evaluated; ужас is compatible with a disaster and not with a new flat. The second is misreading «да ладно» as a request to stop talking. Diagnostic: look at what preceded it. After news it is disbelief and wants confirmation; after an apology it is dismissal and wants a change of subject. The third is register, and it runs in both directions: класс to a professor sounds like a student who has forgotten where she is, while «вот это да» in a formal meeting sounds theatrical. A fourth, subtler error is punctuation and prosody in writing: learners write «Да ладно!!!» for dismissal, which turns a release into a shout, when the dismissal sense usually needs no exclamation mark at all. The repair for all four is the same habit: identify the evaluation direction and strength before choosing the word, and check the relationship before choosing the register.
depth.application: Take five pieces of news from your own week, two good, one bad, one surprising and one neutral, and write each one as a single Russian sentence of six to eight words. Under each, write two reactions from this lesson and one that would misfire, and say in English why it would misfire. Read the five aloud with the intonation you would use, and record them if you can, then listen for whether the disbelief «да ладно» and the dismissal «да ладно» actually sound different in your voice. Most learners produce only the high version, which is why their dismissal reads as incredulity. Next, find one Russian voice message or video clip of two minutes and transcribe only the reactions, ignoring the content. You will end up with a list of eight to twelve items and a sense of how often they occur, which is the quantity that no textbook conveys. The task takes thirty minutes and produces a personal reaction inventory with the misfires marked.
depth.summary: Reactions are evaluations delivered at the point of receipt, and each of the seven carries a direction and a strength. «Да ладно» is disbelief after news and dismissal after an apology, and only the context tells them apart. «Серьёзно» questions the speaker's seriousness, «вот это да» admires without ambiguity, «ничего себе» is high arousal with the direction supplied by tone. класс is peer-level approval, ужас is strong condemnation, and ой is the soft pre-apology. The two noun-derived items, класс and ужас, keep the flavour of their nouns, which is why one sounds like student speech and the other like distress. Read reactions before you produce them, keep ужас for disasters, keep класс for peers, and remember that in writing the exclamation mark is a register choice, not decoration.

lessons.title: Softening a yes and a no: согласен and согласна, ну не знаю, может быть, вряд ли, наоборот and дело в том, что
lessons.explanation: Russian disagreement is usually not done by negating. It is done by moving down a scale of certainty, and the scale is the grammar of this lesson. At the top sits agreement, «Согласен» (sag-LA-sen), 'I agree', said by a man, and «Согласна» (sag-LAS-na) said by a woman. These are short-form adjectives, not verbs, which is why they agree in gender and number rather than in person: «Я согласен» (ya sag-LA-sen), «Я согласна» (ya sag-LAS-na), «Мы согласны» (my sag-LAS-ny). The full form согласный (sag-LAS-ny) exists but belongs to written and official style, where it means 'agreeing' or, of sounds, describes a consonant; in speech the short form is the norm. Dropping the pronoun is normal in speech and slightly reduces the weight of the statement: «Согласен, но есть вопрос» (sag-LA-sen, no yest vap-ROS), 'agreed, but there is a question'. One homonym deserves a note because it confuses learners at exactly this point. согласно (sag-LAS-na) is also a preposition governing the dative, meaning 'according to', as in «согласно приказу» (sag-LAS-na pree-KA-zoo), 'according to the order'. It is pronounced identically to the feminine short adjective, so only the case of the following word tells you which one you are hearing. Below agreement on the scale sit four hedges that every Russian speaker uses daily. «Ну не знаю» (noo ne ZNA-yoo), 'well, I don't know', reports doubt and nothing more; it is the softest way to withhold agreement, and it invites the other person to keep talking. «Может быть» (MO-zhet byt), 'maybe', is a possibility judgement, and in fast speech it shrinks to «может» (MO-zhet), which is acceptable among peers and too casual in writing. «Вряд ли» (vryat lee), 'hardly, unlikely', is a negative prediction rather than a doubt, and the English Wiktionary entry gives the senses exactly: 'I doubt it, (it is) unlikely, probably not', with the example «Вряд ли они придут» (vryat lee a-NEE pree-DOOT), 'it is unlikely that they will come'. Note the syntax: вряд ли is followed by the future perfective when the prediction is about a future event, and by the past when it is about the past, «Вряд ли он успел» (vryat lee on oos-PYEL), 'he is unlikely to have made it'. «Наоборот» (na-a-ba-ROT), 'on the contrary', does something different from all of these: it corrects an inference. It does not soften, it reverses, and it is used when the other person has drawn the wrong conclusion from something true. The distinction from напротив (na-PRO-teef) matters, because напротив is spatial, 'opposite, across the way', and only in formal prose also means 'on the contrary'. Saying «Магазин напротив» (ma-ga-ZEEN na-PRO-teef) means the shop is across the street; «Магазин наоборот» is not a sentence a Russian would produce. The last item is the explanation frame, «Дело в том, что» (DYE-la f tom, shto), 'the thing is that'. It introduces the reason after a soft refusal and converts a bare no into a position with grounds. «Дело в том, что я уже занят» (DYE-la f tom, shto ya oo-ZHE za-NYAT), 'the thing is that I am already busy', is warmer than «Я занят» (ya ZA-NYAT) because it treats the other person as entitled to the reason. The scale, then, runs from согласен through скорее да (ska-REE-ye da), 'probably yes', может быть, ну не знаю and вряд ли to a plain нет (nyet). Fluency in this area is not knowing more words for 'no'; it is knowing where on the scale a given relationship puts you, and being able to move one step rather than three.
lessons.example: A meeting about a launch date, four turns, each hedged differently. «Я думаю, мы успеем к пятнице». (ya DOO-ma-yoo, my oos-PYE-yem k PYA-tee-tse.) 'I think we will make it by Friday.' «Согласен, но есть вопрос по тестированию». (sag-LA-sen, no yest vap-ROS pa tees-tee-ra-va-nee-yu.) 'Agreed, but there is a question about testing.' «Ну не знаю, тестирование обычно дольше». (noo ne ZNA-yoo, tees-tee-ra-va-nee-ye a-BYCH-na DOL-she.) 'Well, I don't know, testing usually takes longer.' «Вряд ли мы успеем, если начнём в среду». (vryat lee my oos-PYE-yem, YES-lee nach-NYOM f SRE-doo.) 'We are unlikely to make it if we start on Wednesday.' «Дело в том, что подрядчик уходит в отпуск». (DYE-la f tom, shto pad-RYAD-cheek oo-KHO-deet v OT-poosk.) 'The thing is that the contractor is going on leave.' Trace the descent. The first response agrees and adds a reservation in the same breath, which is the «согласен, но» pattern and the most common move in Russian meetings. The second does not disagree at all; it reports a doubt and supports it with a general truth about testing, which leaves the original proposal standing but weakened. The third is the first real prediction, and it is conditional: вряд ли plus a condition. The fourth supplies the reason, and it arrives only after the doubt, which is the normal order. Now the same content as a written note. «Сроки вызывают сомнения: тестирование обычно занимает больше времени, а подрядчик уходит в отпуск». (SRO-kee vy-zy-VA-yoot sam-NYE-nee-ya: tees-tee-ra-va-nee-ye a-BYCH-na za-nee-MA-yet BOL-she VRYE-mee-nee, a pad-RYAD-cheek oo-KHO-deet v OT-poosk.) 'The deadlines are doubtful: testing usually takes longer, and the contractor is going on leave.' The written version has no hedges at all, because writing replaces the scale with a structure: a claim, a colon, and two grounds. That substitution is the register skill, and it is the same one lesson 141 applied to fillers.
lessons.question: You want to say that a colleague probably will not come to a meeting. You write «Может быть, он не придёт». What have you said, and what should you say?
lessons.answer: You have said that his absence is one possibility among others, which is weaker than you intended; for a negative prediction use «Вряд ли он придёт» (vryat lee on pree-DYOT), 'he is unlikely to come', or «Скорее всего, он не придёт» (ska-REE-ye fsy-VO, on ne pree-DYOT), 'most likely he will not come'.
lessons.distractor: The sentence is correct and means 'probably he will not come', because может быть expresses probability.
lessons.correction: может быть expresses possibility, not probability, and the difference is the whole point of the scale. Possibility leaves the outcome open in both directions; probability commits you to one. If the meeting is being planned around his attendance, «может быть» tells the organiser nothing, whereas «вряд ли» tells her to plan without him. The repair also has a grammatical side: вряд ли takes the future perfective for a future prediction, so «Вряд ли он придёт», not «Вряд ли он будет приходить» (vryat lee on BOO-deet pree-ha-DEET), which would mean that his habitual visits are unlikely. The English Wiktionary entry lists вряд ли under the particle heading with the gloss 'probably not', which is exactly the strength you needed.

depth.definitions: A short-form adjective is the predicative form of an adjective, agreeing in gender and number but not in person, which is why согласен, согласна, согласно and согласны pattern like a predicate rather than a verb. A hedge is a word or phrase that lowers the strength of a claim. A scalar account of disagreement treats the available responses as points on one scale of certainty rather than as separate speech acts. Face is the social want to be approved of and unimpeded, and politeness theory uses it to explain why a refusal is phrased as a reduced claim rather than as a negation. An inference marker is a word that presents a statement as following from what precedes, which is what наоборот reverses. Prerequisites: the case system supplies the dative after согласно, lesson 87 supplied the formal four-move disagreement, and lesson 104 supplied бы, which is the particle inside может быть and would be inside a conditional version of the same hedge.
depth.mechanism: The mechanism is certainty transfer. Instead of saying 'I disagree', which asserts a proposition and puts the other person in the wrong, the speaker says how likely something is, which asserts a probability and leaves the other person free to argue about evidence. That is why the hedges are not euphemisms for no: they are genuinely different claims, and the conversation that follows them is different. «Ну не знаю» invites more information. «Может быть» invites a decision about whether to wait. «Вряд ли» invites a plan B. Only нет invites a defence. The scale also explains the grammar. Agreement is an adjective because it describes the speaker's state, not an action. Doubt is a negated verb of knowledge. Prediction is a particle that takes the future perfective because it is about a bounded outcome. Correction is an adverb because it modifies the relation between two statements. Each form matches the kind of claim being made, which is why translating the English words produces the wrong strength even when it produces the right meaning.
depth.secondExample: A family exchange, where the same scale is used to refuse an invitation without a quarrel. «Поедем в воскресенье на дачу?» (pa-YE-dem v vas-kree-SYE-nee-ye na DA-choo?) 'Shall we go to the dacha on Sunday?' «Согласна, только давай пораньше». (sag-LAS-na, TOL-ka da-VAY pa-RAN-she.) 'Agreed, only let us go earlier.' «А ты, Дима?» (a ty, DEE-ma?) 'And you, Dima?' «Ну не знаю. Вряд ли получится». (noo ne ZNA-yoo. VRYAT lee pa-LOO-cheet-sya.) 'Well, I don't know. Maybe, it is unlikely to work out.' «Дело в том, что у меня в субботу смена». (DYE-la f tom, shto oo mee-NYA f soo-BO-too SMYE-na.) 'The thing is that I have a shift on Saturday.' «Жаль. Наоборот, думали, ты нас повезёшь». (ZHAL. na-a-ba-ROT, DOO-ma-lee, ty nas pa-vee-ZYOSH.) 'A pity. We thought the opposite, that you would drive us.' Three things are happening. First, the refusal is stacked: «ну не знаю», then «вряд ли», then the reason. A Russian speaker often stacks in exactly this way when the refusal is social rather than logistical, and the stack is not indecision, it is politeness. Second, the reason arrives last and is factual, which is the «дело в том» frame. Third, «наоборот» corrects an assumption about the plan rather than contradicting a person: the family assumed he would drive, and наоборот says the assumption was backwards. A learner who says «Нет, я не поеду» first and explains afterwards has the same information and a different conversation.
depth.mistake: Four errors recur. The first is gender: a woman who says «Я согласен» sounds like a learner reading from a phrasebook, because the adjective must agree. Diagnostic: check the subject, not the speaker's own gender, since «Она согласна» and «Он согласен» follow the subject. The second is confusing может быть with вряд ли, as in the question, which under-commits or over-commits the prediction. Diagnostic: ask what the other person should do differently after hearing you; if the answer is 'nothing', a possibility word was the wrong choice. The third is using наоборот as a spatial word, producing «Магазин наоборот» for 'the shop opposite'; the spatial word is напротив. Diagnostic: if you can point at it, it is напротив. The fourth is punctuation with дело в том, что: Russian requires a comma before что and normally sets the whole frame off with a comma after что only when the clause continues, «Дело в том, что, если мы опоздаем, поезд уйдёт» (DYE-la f tom, shto, YES-lee my a-paz-DA-yem, PO-yezd oo-DYOT), which is heavy and best avoided in speech by stopping after что. There is also a transfer error for speakers of Spanish, who use quizá and tal vez across a wider range than может быть covers, and who therefore under-use вряд ли when a negative prediction is needed.
depth.application: Write four versions of one refusal, all about the same invitation, and label each with the relationship it suits: a close friend, a colleague, a client, and someone senior to you. Use one item from the scale in each, and make the reason explicit in at least two of them. Then reverse the exercise: take a real refusal you have made in Russian in the past month and rewrite it three ways, one step softer, one step firmer, and one step more formal. Read all three aloud and notice which one you would actually say. Finally, build a personal scale chart with five rungs, write the Russian for each rung, and beside each write the English sentence you would have used, so that you can see where your English habits push you too far up or too far down. The chart takes twenty minutes and is more useful than a list of connectives, because it records your own calibration rather than the language's.
depth.summary: Agreement is an adjective that agrees with the subject, so согласен and согласна are not interchangeable and the full form согласный belongs to written style. согласно is also a preposition meaning 'according to', and the homophony with the feminine short form is resolved only by the case that follows. Disagreement is a scale, not a negation: ну не знаю reports doubt, может быть reports possibility, вряд ли reports a negative prediction and takes the future perfective, наоборот corrects an inference rather than contradicting a person, and дело в том, что supplies the reason after a soft refusal. Move one rung at a time, and in writing replace the whole scale with a claim plus explicit grounds, because a report has no face to save.

lessons.title: Opening and closing small talk: как дела, что нового, как прошло, ладно, до связи and созвонимся
lessons.explanation: Small talk in Russian is shorter than most learners expect, and its formulae are more fixed. The English Wikipedia article on phatic expressions supplies the concept: an utterance whose main job is to maintain the channel rather than to convey information. «Как дела?» (kak dee-LA), 'how are things?', is the standard Russian phatic opener, and it behaves like its English counterpart in one respect and unlike it in another. It behaves alike in that the expected answer is short and positive-leaning: «Нормально» (nar-MAL-na), 'fine', «Неплохо» (neep-LO-ha), 'not bad', «Всё хорошо» (vsyo ha-ra-SHO), 'all good'. It behaves differently in that Russian has a second, more specific opener that English lacks a clean equivalent for, «Что нового?» (shto NO-va-va), 'what is new?', which genuinely invites a piece of news and is answered with one, «Да ничего особенного» (da nee-chee-VO a-SO-ben-na-va), 'nothing special', or with a single item. A third opener names an event: «Как прошло?» (kak prash-LO), 'how did it go?'. This one is elliptical, and the ellipsis is the grammar point of the lesson. прошло is the neuter past of пройти (pray-TEE), 'to pass, to go through', and it agrees with the event being asked about, which must already be present in the conversation. Ask «Как прошло?» two days after a colleague's exam and she will pause, because no neuter event has been mentioned. Name it and the question works: «Как прошёл экзамен?» (kak prash-OL eg-ZA-men), 'how did the exam go?', «Как прошла встреча?» (kak prash-LA VSTRYE-cha), 'how did the meeting go?', «Как прошли выходные?» (kak prash-LEE vy-khad-NY-ye), 'how was the weekend?'. The three endings, -о, -а and -и, are the whole agreement system of the past tense doing its ordinary work, and getting them wrong is the most common beginner error in this formula. The openers have a social radius. «Как дела?» works with anyone from a neighbour to a colleague. «Как жизнь?» (kak ZHEEZN), 'how is life?', is intimate and slightly older-sounding, and it is wrong with a stranger. «Как сам?» (kak SAM), 'how are you yourself?', is warm and informal. «Как вы?» (kak VY) is the вы version and is safe at work. The closers are equally fixed, and they come in pairs. The first move is a pre-closing, usually «Ладно» (LAD-na), 'right then', «Ну всё» (noo VSYO), 'that's it then', or «Всё, я побежал» (VSYO, ya pa-bee-ZHAL), 'right, I'm off', which the speaker says to announce that no new topic is coming. The second move is the farewell, and its form depends on the channel: «До связи» (da SVYA-zee), 'until we are in touch', for the phone or messages; «До встречи» (da VSTRYE-chee), 'until we meet', when a meeting is fixed; «До завтра» (da ZAF-tra), 'until tomorrow', when the date is known. Two verbs do most of the work of arranging the next contact. «Созвонимся» (saz-VO-neem-sya), 'we will be in touch by phone', is the perfective future first person plural of созвониться (sa-zva-NEET-sya), a reciprocal verb, which is why the -ся is there: the action is mutual. «Спишемся» (spee-SHEM-sya), 'we will message each other', does the same for written channels, from списаться (spee-SAT-sya). «На связи» (na SVYA-zee), 'in touch', is a short sign-off that promises availability without fixing a time. The mechanics of closing are worth stating explicitly because learners tend to get them wrong in a specific way. Conversation analysis describes closing as a coordinated sequence: one party proposes the end, the other accepts, and only then does the farewell happen. Russian does this with ладно or ну всё as the proposal and до связи as the acceptance plus farewell. If you say до связи without a pre-closing, the other person may hear it as abrupt; if you raise a new topic after ладно, you have broken the proposal and the conversation restarts awkwardly. The safest closing for a learner is two moves: «Ладно, мне пора. До связи» (LAD-na, mnye pa-RA. da SVYA-zee), 'right, I have to go. Until we are in touch'. It names the reason, proposes the end and signs off, in nine syllables.
lessons.example: A corridor exchange, then a phone closing. «Привет. Как дела?» (pree-VYET. kak dee-LA?) 'Hi. How are things?' «Нормально, а у тебя?» (nar-MAL-na, a oo tee-BYA?) 'Fine, and you?' «Да ничего особенного. Что нового?» (da nee-chee-VO a-SO-ben-na-va. shto NO-va-va?) 'Nothing special. What's new?' «Слушай, вчера сдал экзамен». (SLOO-shay, fchee-RA zdal eg-ZA-men.) 'Listen, I passed the exam yesterday.' «Ого! Как прошёл?» (a-GO! kak prash-OL?) 'Wow! How did it go?' «Лучше, чем думал». (LOOT-she, chem DOO-mal.) 'Better than I thought.' The exchange is four turns and thirty seconds, and it contains the whole opener system: the phatic question, the reciprocal question, the news invitation, the announcement, the event-specific follow-up with correct masculine agreement, and an evaluation. Nothing is reported in detail, and nothing needs to be. Now a telephone closing. «Ладно, я на встречу опаздываю». (LAD-na, ya na FSTRYE-choo a-paz-DY-va-yoo.) 'Right, I am running late for a meeting.' «Поняла. Созвонимся вечером?» (pa-nee-LA. saz-VO-neem-sya VYE-chee-ram?) 'Got it. Shall we talk on the phone this evening?' «Давай. До связи». (da-VAY. da SVYA-zee.) 'Let's. Until we are in touch.' «Пока». (pa-KA.) 'Bye.' Three things are happening. The pre-closing names a reason, which is the polite form of the proposal. созвонимся is offered as a question, which turns the arrangement into a shared decision. до связи and пока are the two farewells, one neutral and one informal, and their pairing is normal: до связи closes the channel, пока closes the person. A learner who ends with «До встречи» on the phone has chosen a farewell that promises a meeting, which is a different commitment.
lessons.question: Two days after a colleague's exam you say «Как прошло?» and she looks puzzled. What went wrong, and what are the three correct forms?
lessons.answer: The question has no antecedent: прошло (prash-LO) is neuter and needs a neuter event already in play, so in a new conversation it is empty; name the event and agree the verb with it, «Как прошёл экзамен?» for a masculine noun, «Как прошла встреча?» for a feminine one and «Как прошли выходные?» for a plural one.
lessons.distractor: Nothing is wrong with the phrase itself, but she expected the вы form, because colleagues at work are always addressed with вы.
lessons.correction: The pronoun is not the problem; the missing noun is. «Как прошло?» is a perfectly good question inside a conversation that has already mentioned the event, and this is why learners hear it constantly and then reproduce it out of context. The past tense agrees with the subject, so the ending carries the gender of the event: -о for neuter, -а for feminine, -и for plural. Your colleague's pause was the search for the missing subject, not a judgement about politeness. The repair is to name the event, and if you are unsure of the gender, use the neutral frame «Как всё прошло?» (kak VSYO prash-LO), 'how did it all go?', where всё is the neuter subject and the agreement is safe.

depth.definitions: A phatic expression is an utterance whose function is to establish or maintain social contact rather than to exchange information, and «как дела» is the standard Russian example. A pre-closing is the move that announces the end of a conversation before the farewell, and it is what ладно and ну всё perform. A reciprocal verb is one with the postfix -ся that describes a mutual action, which is why созвониться means 'to call each other' rather than 'to call'. Ellipsis is the omission of a word that the context supplies, and «как прошло» is elliptical because the subject is omitted and must be recovered from the situation. A sign-off is a formula that ends a message or call and names the channel of the next contact. Prerequisites: the past tense agreement of lesson 8, the aspect pair system that makes созвонимся a future perfective, and the register split of lesson 82, which explains why the same closing has a formal and an informal variant.
depth.mechanism: The mechanism of small talk is the exchange of a low-cost token that costs the speaker little and signals willingness to maintain the relationship. Russian makes the token shorter than English does, and it compensates by making the follow-up more specific: «что нового» invites an item, «как прошло» invites an evaluation of a named event, and the answer is expected to be one clause. That is why a long answer to «как дела» is a register error rather than a grammatical one: it treats a token as a request. The closing works by a different mechanism, which is coordination. A conversation cannot end unilaterally without appearing to break it, so one speaker proposes the end and the other accepts, and the farewell is the ratification. The pre-closing is the proposal, and its fixed phrases are recognisable precisely so that the other person can accept them without ambiguity. The two mechanisms together explain the shape of the whole lesson: open with a token, close with a proposal, and put the content in the middle where it belongs.
depth.secondExample: A workplace opening where the same tokens carry a different weight. «Добрый день, Ирина Петровна. Как вы?» (DOB-ry dyen, ee-REE-na peet-ROV-na. kak VY?) 'Good afternoon, Irina Petrovna. How are you?' «Спасибо, хорошо. А вы как?» (spa-SEE-ba, ha-ra-SHO. a vy kak?) 'Thank you, well. And you?' «Тоже нормально. Что нового у вас в отделе?» (TO-zhe nar-MAL-na. shto NO-va-va oo vas at-DYE-le?) 'Also fine. What is new in your department?' «Готовим отчёт, но это долго». (ga-TO-veem at-CHOT, no EH-ta DOL-ga.) 'We are preparing the report, but it is taking a long time.' «Понятно. Ладно, не буду мешать. До связи». (pa-NYAT-na. LAD-na, ne BOO-doo mee-SHAT. da SVYA-zee.) 'I see. Right, I won't disturb you. Until we are in touch.' Four register decisions are visible. The greeting uses the first name plus patronymic and the вы pronoun, which is the default at work with someone older or more senior. The question is «как вы», not «как дела», because the pronoun is explicit and the form is slightly more careful. The news question is addressed to the department rather than to the person, which keeps the exchange professional without becoming cold. The closing uses ладно plus a reason and до связи, which is neutral across channels. Replace any one of the four with its informal counterpart and the exchange changes relationship rather than content, which is the test of whether a register choice has been made correctly.
depth.mistake: Four errors recur. The first is answering «как дела» with a report, which holds the other person in a conversation she did not open; the reply is one word plus a reciprocal question. The second is using «как прошло» without an antecedent, as in the question; the repair is to name the event or to use «как всё прошло». The third is agreement in the named version, producing «как прошла экзамен» or «как прошёл встреча», which sounds like a beginner even when everything else is fluent. Diagnostic: find the noun, decide its gender, then choose -о, -а or -и. The fourth is the channel error in closings: «до встречи» on the phone, «до связи» in a letter, or «пока» to a client. Diagnostic: ask what the next contact actually is, a call, a meeting or a message, and pick the formula that names it. A fifth, purely social error affects learners from cultures with longer small talk: adding a personal question about salary, family or health after «как дела» is read as intrusive in a Russian workplace, where the phatic token is not an invitation to intimacy.
depth.application: Write two versions of the same thirty-second corridor exchange, one with a colleague you address as ты and one with a manager you address as вы, using the openers and closers from this lesson and nothing else. Then record both and listen for whether the вы version is actually slower and more complete, because that is what the register difference sounds like. Next, list every closing you have used in Russian in the past month and classify each by channel: call, message, meeting, letter. You will probably find that you use one formula everywhere, which is the habit this lesson is designed to break. Finally, write a four-line message that opens with «что нового», answers it in one clause, and closes with «до связи», then send it to a Russian-speaking contact if you have one. The task takes twenty-five minutes and produces a pair of scripts you can reuse.
depth.summary: Small talk is a token exchange, and Russian tokens are short: «как дела» expects «нормально» and a reciprocal question, «что нового» expects one item of news, and «как прошло» expects a named event whose gender decides the ending of the verb. Closings are coordinated in two moves, a pre-closing with ладно or ну всё and a farewell chosen by channel, до связи for the phone, до встречи for a meeting, до завтра for a fixed date. созвонимся and спишемся are reciprocal perfective futures that arrange the next contact, and на связи is the short promise of availability. The register radius of each formula is part of its meaning: как жизнь is intimate, как вы is careful, and пока is for people you would also address as ты.

lessons.title: Invitations and arrangements: давай, пойдём, в субботу сможешь, я за, я пас and какие планы
lessons.explanation: An invitation in Russian is a proposal of joint action, and the grammar makes that explicit. The two frames are «Давай» (da-VAY) and «Пойдём» (pay-DYOM), and both are plural in form even when one person is being invited, because the action is to be done together. Cornell's Beginning Russian Grammar states the rule for the first frame with unusual precision: use давай plus the infinitive for imperfective verbs, and давай plus the first person plural non-past for perfective verbs. So «Давай смотреть» (da-VAY smat-RYET), 'let's watch', takes the imperfective infinitive, while «Давай посмотрим» (da-VAY pa-SMOT-reem), 'let's have a look', takes the perfective first person plural. The choice between them is the ordinary aspect choice in miniature: the imperfective presents the activity, the perfective presents a completed episode of it. That is why «Давай пить кофе» (da-VAY PEET KO-fe) sounds like a proposal to take up coffee drinking as a habit, while «Давай выпьем кофе» (da-VAY VY-pyeem KO-fe), 'let's have a coffee', is the invitation a colleague expects. The second frame, «Пойдём» (pay-DYOM), 'let's go', is the first person plural of пойти (pay-TEE) and it is used without давай, especially with verbs of motion, which is the exception Cornell notes explicitly: «Пойдём в кино» (pay-DYOM f kee-NO), 'let's go to the cinema', needs no давай at all. Its polite and plural form is «Пойдёмте» (pay-DYOM-tye), and its very informal twin is «Пошли» (pash-LEE), historically a past tense used as an imperative, which is fine among friends and wrong with a manager. давай has a second life that surprises learners: it is also the agreement word and the goodbye. «Давай» as an answer means 'okay, let's do it', and at the end of a phone call it means 'right, bye'. The intonation is what distinguishes the three uses: a rising давай opens a proposal, a flat давай accepts one, and a falling давай with a pause closes a call. The availability question has its own fixed shape, «В субботу сможешь?» (f soo-BO-too SMO-zhesh), literally 'on Saturday will you be able', with the infinitive omitted because the proposal supplies it. The answer mirrors the modal: «Смогу» (sma-GOO), 'I will be able', or «Не смогу» (ne sma-GOO), 'I won't be able'. The verdict pair is «Я за» (ya ZA), 'I'm in', literally 'I am for', and «Я пас» (ya PAS), 'I'm out', from the card game sense of пас, 'pass'. Both are informal and both are friendly; a softer neutral option is «Я не против» (ya ne PRO-teef), 'I don't mind', which agrees without enthusiasm. Plans are asked about with «Какие планы?» (ka-KEE-ye PLA-ny), 'what plans', and the day goes in the accusative after на: «Какие планы на субботу?» (ka-KEE-ye PLA-ny na soo-BO-too). The arrangement itself uses в plus the accusative for both the day and the hour, «в субботу в семь» (f soo-BO-too f syem), 'on Saturday at seven', and the meeting point takes у plus the genitive, «у входа» (oo FHO-da), 'at the entrance'. Confirmation is a single word, «Договорились» (da-ga-va-REE-lees), 'agreed', and it is the word that turns a plan into a commitment. Cancelling has its own formula, «Планы поменялись» (PLA-ny pa-mee-NYA-lees), 'the plans changed', followed by «Давай перенесём» (da-VAY pee-ree-nee-SYOM), 'let's move it'. The whole sequence has four moves, availability, proposal, verdict, confirmation, and the order matters because each move depends on the one before it.
lessons.example: A four-move arrangement, then the same plan collapsing. «Слушай, какие планы на субботу?» (SLOO-shay, ka-KEE-ye PLA-ny na soo-BO-too?) 'Listen, what are your plans for Saturday?' «Да ничего. А что?» (da nee-chee-VO. a SHTO?) 'Nothing much. Why?' «Давай сходим в кино?» (da-VAY s-HO-deem f kee-NO?) 'Shall we go to the cinema?' «Я за. Во сколько?» (ya ZA. va SKOL-ka?) 'I'm in. At what time?' «В семь у входа». (f syem oo FHO-da.) 'At seven at the entrance.' «Договорились». (da-ga-va-REE-lees.) 'Agreed.' Five turns and the plan exists. Note the grammar of each move. The availability question uses какие планы на plus the accusative. The proposal uses давай with the perfective first person plural сходим, because the cinema trip is a bounded episode. The verdict is the fixed pair member я за. The time uses в семь, and the place у входа. The confirmation is договорились, a past tense plural that functions as a performative: saying it makes the agreement. Now the collapse. «Слушай, я не смогу в субботу». (SLOO-shay, ya ne sma-GOO f soo-BO-too.) 'Listen, I won't be able to on Saturday.' «Жаль. Давай в воскресенье?» (ZHAL. da-VAY v vas-kree-SYE-nee-ye?) 'A pity. Shall we do Sunday?' «Давай. Только не утром». (da-VAY. TOL-ka ne OOT-ram.) 'Let's. Only not in the morning.' «Хорошо, в час дня». (ha-ra-SHO, f chas dnya.) 'Fine, at one in the afternoon.' «Записал». (za-pee-SAL.) 'Noted.' The repair does not start over: it keeps the proposal frame, changes one term and closes with a different confirmation, записал, which is what you say when you have written the details down. That substitution of записал for договорились is the sign that the plan has moved from talk to calendar.
lessons.question: You invite a colleague for coffee and say «Давай пить кофе». She smiles and says it sounds like a habit. What is the error, and what should you say?
lessons.answer: давай with the imperfective infinitive presents the activity rather than one episode, so «Давай пить кофе» (da-VAY PEET KO-fe) means something like 'let's take up drinking coffee'; the invitation is «Давай выпьем кофе» (da-VAY VY-pyeem KO-fe) or «Пойдём выпьем кофе» (pay-DYOM VY-pyeem KO-fe), with the perfective.
lessons.distractor: The error is the missing pronoun, because давай must be followed by мы: «Давай мы пить кофе».
lessons.correction: давай is already the first person plural imperative and it does not take a pronoun; adding мы is ungrammatical here. The error is aspect. Cornell's rule is that давай takes the imperfective infinitive for an activity and the perfective first person plural for a completed episode, so the aspect you choose decides whether the proposal is about a habit or about one coffee. «Давай пить кофе» is what a friend might say on the first morning of a holiday, and it is heard as a programme. «Давай выпьем кофе» is the fifteen-minute invitation. The same contrast explains «Давай встречаться» (da-VAY fstree-CHA-t-sya), 'let's go out together', which is a proposal of a relationship, against «Давай встретимся» (da-VAY FSTRYE-teem-sya), 'let's meet', which is a proposal of one meeting.

depth.definitions: A joint-action imperative is an imperative whose plural form includes the speaker, which is why давай and пойдём mean 'let us' rather than 'you do it'. Aspect is the grammatical distinction between an activity viewed in its course and an episode viewed as complete, and it is the variable that decides the form after давай. A performative is an utterance that brings about what it says, which is what договорились does when it closes an arrangement. Ellipsis is the omission of a recoverable word, which is what happens in «в субботу сможешь» where the infinitive is supplied by the proposal. A verdict pair is a fixed set of two opposite responses used in the same slot, and «я за» and «я пас» are the informal pair in this lesson. Prerequisites: the imperative forms of lesson 79, the aspect system of lesson 7, and the motion verbs of lesson 8, since пойдём is a form of пойти and its use without давай is a motion-verb exception.
depth.mechanism: The mechanism of an invitation is the sharing of agency. A question such as «Ты хочешь в кино?» asks the other person to report a desire, which puts her in the position of deciding alone and makes refusal a statement about herself. A joint-action form such as «Пойдём в кино» proposes that the speaker is also going, so refusal declines a shared plan rather than rejecting a person. That is why the frames are plural and why давай is not optional decoration. The aspect choice then decides what kind of shared thing is proposed: an activity with no boundary, which is a commitment of time and habit, or an episode with a boundary, which is a diary entry. The verdict pair works because it is binary and playful: я за and я пас come from the language of games, so a refusal is coded as a move in a game rather than as a rejection. The confirmation word completes the mechanism by converting a proposal that both parties have accepted into a commitment that neither needs to remember alone.
depth.secondExample: A trickier invitation, where the proposal has to survive a refusal of the first term. «Может, встретимся на неделе?» (MO-zhet, FSTRYE-teem-sya na nee-DYE-le?) 'Perhaps we could meet during the week?' «Давай. Когда тебе удобно?» (da-VAY. kag-DA tee-BYE oo-DOB-na?) 'Let's. When is convenient for you?' «Не знаю. В среду после работы?» (ne ZNA-yoo. v SRE-doo PO-sle ra-BO-ty?) 'I don't know. Wednesday after work?' «В среду не смогу, у меня английский». (v SRE-doo ne sma-GOO, oo mee-NYA an-GLEE-skeey.) 'I can't on Wednesday, I have English.' «Тогда в четверг?» (tag-DA f cheet-VYERK?) 'Thursday, then?' «В четверг я за». (f cheet-VYERK ya ZA.) 'Thursday I'm in.' Four observations. The opening uses «может» plus the perfective first person plural, which is a softer invitation than давай because it presents the meeting as a possibility rather than a proposal. The acceptance is bare давай, the flat intonation version. The refusal of Wednesday uses не смогу and then gives a reason, which is the same three-part refusal pattern as lesson 143. The alternative is offered by the other party with тогда, which marks it as a consequence of the refusal rather than a new proposal. Nothing is repeated, and the arrangement converges in six turns, which is what the machinery is for.
depth.mistake: Four errors recur. The first is aspect after давай, producing «Давай пить кофе» for a single coffee or «Давай выпьем кофе» for a standing arrangement; diagnostic: ask whether the plan has an end, and if it does, use the perfective. The second is putting давай before пойдём, as in «Давай пойдём», which is not ungrammatical but is redundant and sounds like a learner doubling the frame; пойдём carries the proposal alone. The third is register: «Пошли» and «Я пас» are peer language, and both can sound flippant to a manager or a client, where «Может, встретимся?» and «К сожалению, не смогу» are the equivalents. The fourth is the arrangement details: learners say «в субботу на семь» (f soo-BO-too na syem) instead of «в субботу в семь», because the time of an event takes в plus the accusative, while на marks a duration, «на семь часов» (na syem cha-SOF), 'for seven hours', and a deadline takes к plus the dative, «к семи часам» (k see-MEE cha-SAM), 'by seven'. A related transfer error affects English speakers, who invite with 'do you want to', and who therefore overuse «Ты хочешь» where a joint-action form is expected; the result is a string of questions that sound like a survey rather than invitations.
depth.application: Write the same invitation three ways: to a close friend, to a colleague, and to someone you address as вы and do not know well. Each version must contain an availability question, a proposal, a verdict slot and a confirmation, and only one of the three may use «я пас». Then write the cancellation of each plan, using «Планы поменялись» and one alternative. Read all six aloud and mark where the register changes, since the words that change are the grammar of the lesson. Finally, keep a one-week arrangement diary in Russian: every plan you make or receive, written as a four-line entry with the day, the hour, the place and the confirmation word. At the end of the week you will have a personal phrasebook of the arrangements you actually make, which is more useful than a list of invitations you might never use.
depth.summary: Invitations are joint-action forms: давай plus the imperfective infinitive for an activity, давай plus the perfective first person plural for an episode, and пойдём for motion without давай. давай also accepts and also says goodbye, and only intonation separates the three. Availability is asked with «в субботу сможешь», the verdict is «я за» or «я пас» among peers and softer formulae elsewhere, and the arrangement takes в plus the accusative for day and hour and у plus the genitive for the meeting point. «Договорились» closes the plan and «записал» confirms that it has been written down. The four moves, availability, proposal, verdict and confirmation, are the whole structure, and their order is what makes a plan survive.
