questions.prompt: A colleague asks you to explain a delay and you start with «Ну, значит, короче, мы не успели». A Russian listener winces. Which of the three fillers is doing the damage, and what should replace the chain?
questions.answer: короче (KO-ro-che) is the problem: it announces compression and carries an impatient, slightly dismissive tone, and three fillers in a row sound like a teenager stalling; one marker plus the fact is enough, for example «Значит, мы не успели» (ZNA-cheet, my ne oos-PYE-lee), 'so, we did not make it'.
questions.distractor: ну (NOO) is the problem, because it is a rude interjection and cannot open a sentence in a work context.
questions.correction: ну (NOO) is the least marked of the three and opens a turn without offence; it is the standard softener before an explanation. The offender is короче (KO-ro-che), which is the comparative of короткий (ka-ROT-keey), 'short', and as a вводное слово it tells the hearer that what follows has been trimmed, usually with the implication that the speaker is tired of explaining. Chaining ну, значит and короче is the real error: each one signals that the speaker is still assembling the answer, so three of them say the answer is not ready. Keep one, usually значит (ZNA-cheet) for an explanation or ну for a concession, and let the content follow.

questions.prompt: You tell a friend that a plan fell through and she answers «Да ладно!» (da LAD-na). You then repeat the whole story in more detail. What have you misunderstood?
questions.answer: «Да ладно!» here is a reaction of surprise or disbelief, roughly 'no way', so the correct response is to confirm briefly, «Правда, всё отменили» (PRAV-da, vsyo at-mee-NEE-lee), 'really, they cancelled everything', not to retell the story.
questions.distractor: «Да ладно!» means 'never mind', so she is telling you to stop talking about the plan.
questions.correction: «Да ладно» has two lives. As a reaction to news it means 'no way, really?', and it invites confirmation, not repetition. As a response to an apology or an offer it means 'never mind, forget it', and that reading requires a different context, usually a favour or an inconvenience rather than a piece of news. What tells them apart is what precedes: after an item of news it is disbelief, after «Извини» (eez-vee-NEE), 'sorry', it is dismissal. Your error was to hear the dismissal sense and answer it with more detail, which reads as insisting on a story the other person has already reacted to. Confirm in one clause and stop.

questions.prompt: At a meeting you disagree with a proposal. You say «Я не согласен» (ya ne sag-LA-sen). A Russian colleague suggests «Ну не знаю» (noo ne ZNA-yoo) instead. Why is the replacement softer, and what does it commit you to?
questions.answer: «Ну не знаю» presents doubt rather than a verdict, so it opens a space for the other side to argue; the cost is that it commits you to nothing, and if you actually oppose the proposal you must add a reason, for example «Ну не знаю, сроки слишком короткие» (noo ne ZNA-yoo, SRO-kee SLEESH-kam ka-ROT-kee-ye), 'well, I don't know, the deadlines are too tight'.
questions.distractor: «Ну не знаю» is simply a more polite way of saying the same refusal, so it can replace «Я не согласен» in every situation without adding anything.
questions.correction: The two do different jobs. «Я не согласен» is a stated position and ends the negotiation of whether you agree. «Ну не знаю» is an epistemic hedge: it reports low confidence, not opposition, and Russian colleagues use it precisely because it does not force the other person to defend a position yet. That is why it is softer, and also why it is weaker. If you leave it alone, the meeting may read your turn as indifference rather than objection. The repair is one clause of reason, which converts doubt into a position without returning to the flat не согласен. Note also the gender pair: a woman says «Я не согласна» (ya ne sag-LAS-na).

questions.prompt: A neighbour says «Как дела?» (kak dee-LA) in the stairwell. You answer with four sentences about your work week. What is wrong, and what would a native reply?
questions.answer: «Как дела» is a greeting formula, not a request for a report; the expected reply is one word or one clause, «Нормально, спасибо» (nar-MAL-na, spa-SEE-ba), 'fine, thanks', optionally with a short reciprocal «А у вас?» (a oo VAS), 'and you?', which is the вы form to a neighbour you do not know well.
questions.distractor: Nothing is wrong, because «Как дела» is a genuine question about your week and a full answer shows that you are friendly.
questions.correction: The formula has been bleached into a greeting, in the same way as 'how are you' in English, and a long answer holds the other person in a conversation she did not open. The grammatical clue is the register of the expected answer: нормально (nar-MAL-na), 'normal, fine', is the default, and it is deliberately non-committal. A full account is appropriate only when the other person asks a real question, «Как прошла неделя?» (kak prash-LA nee-DYE-lya), 'how did the week go?', which names the period and therefore asks about it. Your error is register rather than grammar, which is why it feels rude without containing a mistake.

questions.prompt: You want to propose cinema on Saturday. Which is the natural Russian move, and what does the reply «Я пас» (ya PAS) mean?
questions.answer: The natural move is «Давай в субботу в кино?» (da-VAY f soo-BO-too f kee-NO), 'let's do cinema on Saturday?', or «Пойдём в субботу в кино?» (pay-DYOM f soo-BO-too f kee-NO); «Я пас» means 'I'm out, count me out', a friendly refusal borrowed from card games, not an objection to the plan.
questions.distractor: The natural move is «Ты хочешь в субботу в кино?» and «Я пас» means 'I'll pass the tickets to someone else'.
questions.correction: «Давай» and «Пойдём» are the two invitation frames, and both are first person plural in form: they propose a joint action rather than ask about the other person's desire, which is why they sound like an invitation and not a survey. Cornell's grammar gives the rule for давай: imperfective infinitive after it, perfective first person plural without it, so «Давай смотреть» (da-VAY smat-RYET), 'let's watch', and «Давай посмотрим» (da-VAY pa-SMOT-reem), 'let's watch it through'. «Я пас» is a set phrase from cards meaning 'I pass', used for declining an invitation without criticising it. «Ты хочешь» is grammatical but puts the decision on the other person and sounds like a test.

units.title: Taken live: the phone and the messenger, the spoken story, humour, the ты and вы switch and a capstone exchange

lessons.title: On the phone and in the messenger: алло, я не слышу, набери мне, скинь, голосовое and the short forms спс, пож, чё
lessons.explanation: The telephone created its own Russian vocabulary, and messaging has added a second layer on top of it. The first word is «Алло» (al-LO), which is a telephone greeting and nothing else. It is never used face to face, and using it to a person standing in front of you is a joke. Its intonation decides the meaning: a rising «Алло?» asks whether anyone is there, and a flat «Алло» answers. On a business line the standard answer is not алло at all but «Иван Петрович слушает» (ee-VAN pee-TRO-veech SLOO-sha-yet), literally 'Ivan Petrovich is listening', a third person formula that names the person answering without using the first person pronoun. The second layer of vocabulary is about the channel failing. «Я не слышу» (ya ne SLY-shoo), 'I cannot hear you', reports a problem at your end, and the impersonal «Вас не слышно» (vas ne SLYSH-na), 'you cannot be heard', is the polite version because it removes the accusation. The contrast between слышать (SLY-shat), 'to perceive sound', and слушать (SLOO-shat), 'to listen', is grammatical and social at once: «Я не слушаю» (ya ne SLOO-sha-yoo) means 'I am not listening to you', which on a call is an insult rather than a repair. Requests about the call use a small set of imperatives. «Набери мне» (na-bee-REE mnye), 'call me', comes from набрать (nab-RAT), 'to dial', whose imperative набери is formed with the stressed -и because the first person singular наберу carries end stress. «Перезвони» (pee-reez-va-NEE), 'call back', is the same pattern from перезвонить. «Набери ещё раз» (na-bee-REE yeshchyo RAZ), 'call again', is the standard repair for a dropped line. The messaging vocabulary is where register becomes visible, because the same act has three names at three levels. At the neutral level a file is sent: «Пришлите, пожалуйста, файл» (preesh-LEE-tye, pa-ZHA-las-ta, FYLE), 'please send the file'. At the peer level it is thrown over: «Скинь файл» (SKEEN FYLE), 'send the file over', from скинуть (SKEE-noot), a perfective verb whose literal sense is 'to throw off' and whose colloquial sense is 'to send, to forward'. The Wiktionary entry derives it transparently as с- plus кинуть (KEE-noot), 'to throw', which is exactly why it feels casual: the metaphor is tossing something across. The same verb covers money, «Скинь мне на карту» (SKEEN mnye na KAR-too), 'transfer it to my card', and links, «Скинь ссылку» (SKEEN SSYL-koo), 'send the link'. A voice message is «голосовое» (ga-la-sa-VO-ye), a clipped neuter adjective from голосовое сообщение (ga-la-sa-VO-ye sa-ap-SHCHYE-ni-ye), 'voice message'. The clipping is itself a register marker: the full phrase belongs to the app's interface, the single word belongs to the conversation. Writing is compressed further. «Спс» stands for спасибо (spa-SEE-ba), 'thanks', «пож» for пожалуйста (pa-ZHA-las-ta), 'please', and «чё» for что (shto), 'what'. The first two are pure abbreviations and are read aloud as the full words, which is why they are harmless between friends and bizarre in a letter: nobody says «спс» out loud. The third is different, because чё is a real pronunciation with its own spelling, and it is marked as substandard in careful speech. It carries a shrug: «Чё?» (CHYO) as 'what?' is confrontational where «Что?» is neutral and «Простите?» (pra-STEE-tye) is polite. The same shrug explains «ничё» (nee-CHO), a reduction of ничего (nee-chee-VO), which can mean 'nothing' or 'it's fine'. The register ladder for a single request runs from «Не могли бы вы прислать файл ещё раз?» (ne mag-LEE by vy pree-SLAT FYLE yeshchyo RAZ), 'could you possibly send the file again', through «Пришлите, пожалуйста, файл ещё раз», through «Скинь файл ещё раз», to «скинь пож» with no verb at all. Each rung removes a syllable of distance and a gram of obligation, and the relationship decides the rung. A last convention belongs to the phone rather than to the words: Russians often begin a call to a friend with «Привет, удобно?» (pree-VYET, oo-DOB-na), 'hi, is now convenient?', which is a request for permission to occupy the next minute. It is shorter than an apology and it does the same work.
lessons.example: A call that keeps failing, then the same failure in writing. «Алло?» (al-LO?) 'Hello?' «Привет, это я. Тебя плохо слышно». (pree-VYET, EH-ta ya. tee-BYA PLO-ha SLYSH-na.) 'Hi, it's me. You are hard to hear.' «Да, я в метро. Я тебе перезвоню». (da, ya v meet-RO. ya tee-BYE pee-reez-va-NYOO.) 'Yes, I am on the metro. I will call you back.' «Хорошо. Или скинь голосовое». (ha-ra-SHO. EE-lee SKEEN ga-la-sa-VO-ye.) 'Fine. Or send a voice message.' «Давай. Наберу через десять минут». (da-VAY. na-bee-ROO CHYE-rez DYE-syat mee-NOOT.) 'Okay. I will call in ten minutes.' Four observations. «Тебя плохо слышно» is impersonal with the accusative of the person, 'you are poorly heard', which is softer than «Я тебя плохо слышу», 'I hear you badly', because it does not name the listener as the one with the problem. «Перезвоню» is the perfective future, so it commits to one return call, while «буду перезванивать» (BOO-doo pee-reez-VA-nee-vat) would promise repeated attempts. «Скинь голосовое» replaces the call with an asynchronous message, which is the specific repair that messaging has added to telephone Russian. «Наберу через десять минут» uses через plus the accusative for a time interval, which is the standard way to schedule the next contact inside a call. Now the written version, same content, peer register. «привет, не слышно. скинь голосовое пож» (pree-VYET, ne SLYSH-na. SKEEN ga-la-sa-VO-ye pozh) 'hi, can't hear. send a voice message pls'. No capital letters, no pronoun, no verb in the last clause, and the whole message is nine words. That is not laziness; it is the register of a channel that expects a reply in seconds.
lessons.question: You write to a client «Скиньте файл, пож» and the reply is cool. What went wrong, and what are the two repairs?
lessons.answer: скинуть is a colloquial verb that treats the file as something tossed across, and «пож» is a written abbreviation of пожалуйста that reads as haste; with a client use «Пришлите, пожалуйста, файл» (preesh-LEE-tye, pa-ZHA-las-ta, FYLE) or, more formal, «Не могли бы вы прислать файл ещё раз?» (ne mag-LEE by vy pree-SLAT FYLE yeshchyo RAZ).
lessons.distractor: The only problem is the missing capital letter, because «скиньте» is a neutral verb for sending a file and «пож» is an accepted abbreviation in business writing.
lessons.correction: Capitalisation is the smallest issue. The verb is the problem: скинуть is literal 'to throw off' and its sending sense is marked colloquial, so in a client letter it reads as treating the transaction as a favour between friends. The abbreviation compounds it, because nobody pronounces «пож», which signals that the writer did not spend the time to type the word. Neither item is rude in itself, and both are normal between colleagues; the error is a register mismatch, which is exactly the kind of mistake that produces a cool reply rather than a complaint. The repair restores the imperative of прислать (pree-SLAT), 'to send', and the full пожалуйста, and the more formal version adds the negative question frame that lesson 143 described as a softener.

depth.definitions: A register is the variety of language appropriate to a situation, and the ladder in this lesson is a register continuum rather than a set of fixed styles. A clipped form is a word formed by cutting a longer phrase, which is how голосовое сообщение becomes голосовое. An abbreviation in writing is a shortening that is read aloud as the full word, which is the status of спс and пож. A substandard form is one that native speakers recognise but do not accept in careful speech, which is the status of чё in most usage guides. An impersonal construction removes the agent, and «вас не слышно» uses it to avoid blaming the listener. Prerequisites: the imperative formation of lesson 79, which explains the -и of набери and перезвони, the слышать and слушать distinction from lesson 146's own explanation, and the register ladder of lesson 82.
depth.mechanism: Telephone Russian is shaped by the absence of shared context. The speakers cannot see each other, so the language develops formulae that establish the channel, test it, repair it and close it, and each formula is short because the channel is expensive in attention. That is why алло exists at all: it is a channel test disguised as a greeting. Messaging changes the economics, because the channel is cheap and asynchronous, so the formulae compress further and the register drops. The compression is not random: it removes exactly the elements that carried politeness in speech, the pronoun, the verb and the full form of пожалуйста, and what remains is the content. That is why the same nine words can be friendly between peers and curt with a client: the missing elements are the politeness, and their absence is read as a statement about the relationship. The mechanism explains the direction of the ladder, from full forms that spend syllables on distance to clipped forms that spend none.
depth.secondExample: A voicemail and a missed call, which is where learners most often freeze. «Вы позвонили Ивану Петровичу. Оставьте сообщение после сигнала». (vy pa-zva-NEE-lee ee-VA-noo pee-TRO-vee-choo. a-STAF-tye sa-ap-SHCHYE-nee-ye PO-sle seeg-NA-la.) 'You have called Ivan Petrovich. Leave a message after the signal.' A learner's reply: «Здравствуйте, это Анна. Я по поводу встречи в четверг. Перезвоните мне, пожалуйста». (zdra-stvooy-tye, EH-ta A-na. ya pa PO-va-doo FSTRYE-chee f cheet-VYERK. pee-reez-va-NEE-tye mnye, pa-ZHA-las-ta.) 'Hello, this is Anna. I am calling about the meeting on Thursday. Please call me back.' The message works because it follows a three-part shape: who is calling, what it is about, what the listener should do. The first part uses «это» plus the name, which is the standard telephone identification, not «я Анна», which sounds like an introduction at a party. The second part uses «по поводу» (pa PO-va-doo) plus the genitive, 'about, regarding', which is the neutral way to name a topic without a full sentence. The third part is the imperative plus пожалуйста, and it names the action rather than the desire. A message that omits the third part leaves the listener unsure whether a reply is expected, which is the most common voicemail failure among learners.
depth.mistake: Four errors recur. The first is answering a personal call with «Слушаю» (SLOO-sha-yoo) in a peer context, which is a business formula and sounds like a call centre; among friends the answer is алло or привет. The second is «Я не слушаю» for a bad line, which is an insult rather than a repair; the correct forms are «Я не слышу» and «Тебя не слышно». The third is register drift in messaging, using скинь, спс and чё upwards to people who have not granted that intimacy. Diagnostic: ask whether you would use the person's first name without a patronymic; if not, the clipped forms are wrong too. The fourth is a spelling error that follows from pronunciation: writing «щё» or «чо» for чё, or «спс» with a Latin с. A fifth error is specific to learners who have learned the phrase «Как дела» well and then answer a business call with it; on the phone the opening is алло or the name formula, and как дела comes after the identification, not before it.
depth.application: Write four versions of one request, to send a file by Friday: a client letter, an internal email to your team, a message to a colleague you address as ты, and a message to a friend. Each version must contain a form of address, a request and a deadline, and only the last two may contain скинь. Then record a one-minute voicemail in Russian using the three-part shape, identify, topic, action, and listen for whether all three parts are audible in the first twenty seconds. Next, take the last ten messages you sent in Russian and mark every clipped form and every abbreviation; for each one, write the full form beside it. The list is your personal register profile, and it usually shows a strong bias in one direction. The whole task takes thirty minutes and produces two artefacts you can reuse, a request template and a voicemail script.
depth.summary: Telephone Russian has its own formulae: алло is a channel test, the business answer names the speaker in the third person, «вас не слышно» repairs a bad line without blaming anyone, and набери, перезвони and набери ещё раз handle the mechanics. Messaging compresses the same acts: скинь is the peer verb for sending, голосовое is the clipped voice message, and спс, пож and чё are written shortenings of спасибо, пожалуйста and что, of which the first two are read as full words and the third is substandard in careful speech. The register ladder runs from «не могли бы вы прислать» to «скинь пож», and each rung removes politeness along with syllables. Match the rung to the relationship, answer a call with алло rather than слушаю unless you are at work, and never say «я не слушаю» when you mean «я не слышу».

lessons.title: Holding a listener through a story: представляешь, короче, в общем, в итоге and the tense switching of spoken narrative
lessons.explanation: A spoken story is not a list of events; it is a performance with a shape, and Russian marks the shape with four words and one grammatical habit. The words are discourse markers, which the English Wikipedia article defines as expressions that manage the relation between parts of a discourse rather than adding content. The habit is tense switching, and it is the part that learners rarely acquire because it is invisible in written texts. Begin with the four markers, because each one does a different job in the architecture. «Представляешь» (preet-stav-LYA-yesh), 'imagine', is the second person singular of представлять (preet-stav-LYAT) used as an appeal to the listener. It pulls her into the scene and licenses detail: after представляешь, a listener expects to be shown something rather than told a conclusion. Its formal and plural form is «представляете» (preet-stav-LYA-ee-tye), and its variant «представь себе» (preet-STAF see-BYE) is slightly more theatrical. «В общем» (VOP-shem), 'basically, so, anyway', comes from общий (OP-shcheey), 'common, general', and its job is to return to the main line after background. In fast speech it fuses into «вобщем» (VOP-shem), which is how it is usually pronounced, and in writing the two words are kept apart. «Короче» (KO-ro-che) is the compression marker, and its job is to announce that detail is being skipped. «В итоге» (veet-TO-ge) comes from итог (ee-TOK), 'result, total', and it announces the outcome. The four form a sequence with a logic: в общем says 'back to the point', короче says 'cutting ahead', в итоге says 'here is how it ended', and представляешь says 'come inside the scene'. Use them in that order and the story has a map. The tense habit is the second half. Spoken Russian narrative commonly opens in the present, «Иду я вчера по улице» (ee-DOO ya fchee-RA pa OO-lee-tse), 'so I am walking down the street yesterday', and this present is not a mistake: it is the historical present, «настоящее историческое» (na-sta-YA-shche-ye ees-ta-REE-chyes-ka-ye), which sets the scene at the moment of telling. The switch to the past marks the events: «Иду я вчера по улице, вижу автобус, а он уже отходит». (ee-DOO ya fchee-RA pa OO-lee-tse, VEE-zhoo af-TO-boos, a on oo-ZHE at-KHO-deet.) 'So I am walking down the street yesterday, I see the bus, and it is already pulling away.' The present verbs hold the scene and the last clause keeps the present because the action is happening before the eyes of the telling. Then the plot moves: «Я побежал, но не успел». (ya pa-bee-ZHAL, no ne oos-PYEL.) 'I ran, but I did not make it.' The past takes over for the sequence of completed events, and the aspect does the rest: побежал is perfective, a single bounded action, while the earlier вижу is imperfective, an ongoing perception. There is one more device worth knowing because it is very Russian and very hard to translate. A sudden action in a story is often marked with как plus the future perfective: «Он как закричит!» (on kak za-kree-CHEET), 'and he suddenly shouted', or «Она как заплачет» (a-NA kak za-PLA-chet), 'and she burst into tears'. The future form does not refer to the future at all; it is a dramatic present that presents the action as arriving without warning. The related construction «взял и ушёл» (vzyal ee oo-SHOL), literally 'took and left', marks a decision taken abruptly, and «вдруг» (vdroog), 'suddenly', does the same work lexically for learners who do not yet trust the future. None of these devices belongs in a written report, where the whole narrative apparatus is replaced by chronology and connectives.
lessons.example: One story, told twice: once with the markers and tense shifts, once flattened. «Представляешь, иду я вчера по улице, вижу автобус, а он уже отходит. Я побежал, но не успел. В общем, опоздал на встречу. Короче, пришлось брать такси, и в итоге я приехал даже раньше». (preet-stav-LYA-yesh, ee-DOO ya fchee-RA pa OO-lee-tse, VEE-zhoo af-TO-boos, a on oo-ZHE at-KHO-deet. ya pa-bee-ZHAL, no ne oos-PYEL. VOP-shem, a-paz-DAL na FSTRYE-choo. KO-ro-che, pree-SHLOOS brat tak-SEE, ee veet-TO-ge ya pree-YE-hal DA-zhe RAN-she.) 'Imagine, so I am walking down the street yesterday, I see the bus, and it is already pulling away. I ran, but did not make it. So, I was late for the meeting. In short, I had to take a taxi, and in the end I arrived even earlier.' Now the flattened version. «Вчера я шёл по улице. Я видел автобус. Автобус отходил. Я бежал, но не успел. Я опоздал на встречу. Я взял такси. Я приехал раньше». (fchee-RA ya SHOL pa OO-lee-tse. ya VEE-del af-TO-boos. af-TO-boos at-ha-DEEL. ya be-ZHAL, no ne oos-PYEL. ya a-paz-DAL na FSTRYE-choo. ya vzyal tak-SEE. ya pree-YE-hal RAN-she.) 'Yesterday I walked down the street. I saw a bus. The bus was pulling away. I ran but did not make it. I was late for the meeting. I took a taxi. I arrived earlier.' Every sentence is grammatical and every verb is correctly inflected, and the story is dead. Four things have been lost. The present-tense scene is gone, so the listener is outside the story rather than inside it. The aspect has flattened, because шёл, видел and бежал are all imperfective and present the events as ongoing, so nothing advances. The markers are gone, so the listener has to infer which clause is background and which is plot. And the absence of короче means the compression is invisible, so the taxi arrives without the sense of a decision. The two versions contain the same facts and are not the same story.
lessons.question: You open a story with «Короче, я вчера опоздал на поезд...» and after thirty seconds your friend says «Ближе к делу» (BLEE-zhe k DYE-loo), 'get to the point'. What did короче promise, and how should you have opened?
lessons.answer: короче (KO-ro-che) promises that detail is being cut, so it belongs at the point where you actually cut, not at the start; open with «Представляешь» (preet-stav-LYA-yesh) or «В общем» (VOP-shem) to set the scene, and save короче for the jump to the outcome.
lessons.distractor: The friend was simply impatient, and короче at the start is the standard way to begin any informal story in Russian.
lessons.correction: Beginning with короче is common among teenagers and it is exactly what makes listeners interrupt, because the word promises compression and then delivers detail. Your friend's «ближе к делу» is the hearer enforcing the promise. The marker system only works if each word is placed where its promise is true: представляешь opens the scene and licenses detail, в общем returns from background to the main line, короче skips ahead, в итоге lands the outcome. A story that opens with короче has spent its compression marker before there is anything to compress, and the listener correctly concludes that the telling will be longer than the promise. The repair is not to delete короче but to move it to the moment where you stop explaining and start concluding.

depth.definitions: A discourse marker is an expression that organises the relation between parts of a discourse rather than contributing propositional content. The historical present is the use of present-tense forms to narrate past events, and it is a stylistic device rather than a tense error. Aspect is the grammatical distinction between an activity viewed in its course and an event viewed as complete, and it is what makes a narrative chain advance. A dramatic future is the use of a future perfective form for a sudden past action, as in «как закричит». Background is the material that sets the scene without advancing the plot, and it is typically imperfective. Prerequisites: the aspect system of lesson 7, the narrative aspect contrast of lesson 79, and the discourse markers introduced at the end of the foundational course, which this lesson turns into a working set for speech.
depth.mechanism: The mechanism is the division of labour between tense and aspect. Tense locates the telling, and aspect locates the event in the story. When a speaker opens in the present, she is saying 'I am showing you this now', and the listener responds by imagining the scene. When she switches to the past perfective, she is saying 'this happened, and it is over', and the listener responds by waiting for the next event. The markers then label the transitions, so the listener does not have to guess. представляешь marks the entry into the scene, в общем marks the exit from background, короче marks the cut, в итоге marks the landing. That is why the markers cluster at transitions and not inside clauses: they are signposts, and a signpost in the middle of a road is useless. The whole apparatus exists because speech is linear and irreversible: a listener cannot go back and re-read, so the speaker has to announce the shape in advance. Writing can rely on paragraphs and headings instead, which is why the same story written down loses the markers and keeps the chronology.
depth.secondExample: A story with a complication, where the markers carry the listener over a jump in time. «В общем, мы решили поехать на дачу. Представляешь, собираемся, а машина не заводится. Короче, час провозились. В итоге поехали на электричке». (VOP-shem, my ree-SHEE-lee pa-YE-hat na DA-choo. preet-stav-LYA-yesh, sa-bee-RA-yem-sya, a ma-SHEE-na ne za-VO-deet-sya. KO-ro-che, chas pra-va-ZEE-lees. veet-TO-ge pa-YE-ha-lee na e-leek-TREECH-kye.) 'So, we decided to go to the dacha. Imagine, we are getting ready, and the car will not start. In short, we fiddled with it for an hour. In the end we went by suburban train.' The first marker returns to the main line after an implied earlier discussion, which the listener never heard, and that is normal: в общем can summarise material that exists only in the speaker's head. The second marker opens the scene at the moment of the problem. The third cuts an hour of futile work with two words, and the cut is the point of the story. The fourth lands the outcome. Note the tense pattern: решили is past perfective because it is a decision, собираемся and не заводится are present because they are the scene, провозились is past perfective because the hour is a completed episode, and поехали is past perfective because it is the outcome. Five clauses, three tenses, and the listener never loses the thread. A learner who tells the same story entirely in the past will produce a correct and lifeless paragraph, which is the failure the example above demonstrated.
depth.mistake: Four errors recur. The first is opening with короче, which spends the compression marker before there is anything to compress and invites exactly the interruption in the question. The second is telling the whole story in the imperfective because the events are in the past and the learner has been taught that the past is the tense of narrative; the result is a scene with no plot. Diagnostic: underline the verbs that advance the story; if they are all imperfective, the story is a description. The third is overusing представляешь in every other sentence, which turns an appeal into a tic and makes the listener feel summoned rather than engaged. The fourth is a comprehension error with the dramatic future: hearing «он как закричит» as a prediction about the future rather than as a past event. The context, usually a past-time setting such as вчера, resolves it, and the particle как before the verb is the signal. A fifth error belongs to writing: importing в итоге and короче into a report as if they were ordinary connectives, where the first is acceptable but slightly conversational and the second is not acceptable at all.
depth.application: Record yourself telling a two-minute story about something that went wrong in the past week, in Russian, using at least three of the four markers and at least one switch into the historical present. Then transcribe it and mark every verb for tense and aspect. You are looking for a chain of perfectives at the points where the story advances and imperfectives where it sets the scene; if the chain is uniform, revise it. Next, rewrite the same story as a written paragraph of five sentences with no markers and no historical present, using chronology and explicit connectives instead. Compare the two and write one sentence in English about what each version can do that the other cannot. Finally, listen to a Russian speaker telling a story for three minutes, for example in an interview or a podcast, and count the markers. The count is usually higher than a learner expects, and it is the best evidence that the markers are structure rather than decoration.
depth.summary: Spoken narrative runs on four markers and one tense habit. представляешь brings the listener into the scene, в общем returns from background to the main line, короче cuts ahead and must be placed where the cut happens, в итоге lands the outcome. The historical present sets the scene, the past perfective advances the plot, and the imperfective holds the background, so a story that stays in one tense has events without shape. The dramatic future after как, as in «он как закричит», marks a sudden past action and is one of the devices that makes Russian storytelling sound Russian. Writing replaces the whole apparatus with chronology and connectives, which is why a report should contain none of these markers.

lessons.title: Humour and irony markers: шутка, да шучу я, ну ты чего, and the ones that do not cross into English
lessons.explanation: Russian humour is signalled in speech by a small set of words whose job is to manage the risk of a joke. A joke is a bid for laughter, and laughter is not guaranteed, so every language has repairs for the moment when the bid fails. Russian repairs are more explicit than English ones and they are more formulaic, which is why a learner who translates them word for word produces something that sounds either defensive or aggressive. The first repair is «Шутка» (SHOOT-ka), 'a joke', from шутить (shoo-TEET), 'to joke'. Said on its own after a line that has not landed, it labels what has just happened, and that labelling is precisely its weakness: a joke that needs a label has failed, and the label makes the failure visible. Russians do say it, and they say it more often in writing, where intonation cannot carry the signal. The second repair is «Да шучу я» (da shoo-CHOO ya), 'I'm joking', with the verb in the first person singular and the pronoun after it, which is the emphatic order. The phrase is usually repeated, «Шучу-шучу» (shoo-CHOO shoo-CHOO), and the repetition is the point: it performs the de-escalation rather than merely stating it. The third item is the one that does not translate. «Ну ты чего» (noo ty chee-VO), literally 'well, what are you', is said to the person who has taken a joke badly, and it combines reproach with affection in a proportion that English has no single phrase for. It means something between 'come on, what's got into you' and 'don't be like that', and its force depends entirely on intonation: a drawn-out rising «ну ты чего-о» with a smile is warm, and a flat «ну ты чего» after a genuine betrayal is a reproach. That double life is why it does not cross: an English learner who translates it as 'what is wrong with you' produces an accusation where the Russian produced an invitation to lighten. Irony has its own markers, and they are mostly negative. «Ну да, конечно» (noo DA, ka-NYESH-na), 'yeah, right, of course', with a flat or drawled delivery, means the opposite of what it says, and it is the standard Russian response to a claim the speaker does not believe. «Ага, сейчас» (a-GA, see-CHAS), 'yeah, right now', refuses a request ironically by pretending to accept it. A single «Конечно» (ka-NYESH-na) with a falling tone can do the same work with no other signal at all. The particles of lesson 102 are also part of the toolkit, because же and -то mark shared assumptions and therefore make irony possible: «Ты же специалист» (ty zhe spee-tsee-a-LEEST), 'you are the expert, after all', can be sincere or sarcastic depending on what follows. There is one lexical trap that belongs in this lesson because it causes real confusion. «Анекдот» (a-neek-DOT) is not an anecdote. It is a joke, usually a short narrative joke with a punchline and often with recurring characters, and the English word 'anecdote' corresponds instead to «случай» (SLOO-chay), 'an incident', or «история» (ees-TO-ree-ya), 'a story'. A learner who offers an anecdote about her weekend after being asked for an анекдот has answered a different question. Two smaller items complete the set. «Смешно» (smeesh-NO), 'funny', is the adjective of the effect rather than the genre, and «мне смешно» (mnye smeesh-NO), 'I find it funny', is a personal judgement that leaves room for disagreement. «Прикол» (pree-KOL) is slang for a joke or a prank, and «блин» (BLEEN), literally 'pancake', is a mild expletive used as a softener or a sigh; both are peer-level and both date quickly.
lessons.example: A joke that fails, and three repairs. «Ты опять забыл ключи? Ну ты и голова!» (ty a-PYAT za-BYL klyu-CHEE? noo ty ee ga-la-VA!) 'You forgot the keys again? You are quite the head!' «Я не голова, я человек». (ya ne ga-la-VA, ya chee-la-VYEK.) 'I am not a head, I am a person.' «Да шучу я, шучу. Просто ты всегда их забываешь». (da shoo-CHOO ya, shoo-CHOO. PRO-sta ty fseg-DA eekh za-by-VA-yesh.) 'I'm joking, joking. It's just that you always forget them.' «Шутки у тебя так себе». (SHOOT-kee oo tee-BYA tak see-BYE.) 'Your jokes are so-so.' «Ну ты чего, обиделся?» (noo ty chee-VO, a-BEE-deel-sya?) 'Come on, are you offended?' The exchange shows the whole apparatus. «Ну ты и голова» is an ironic compliment, built on «ну ты и» plus a noun, and it is the frame that most often misfires because the same frame is sincere in other contexts. The repair «да шучу я, шучу» repeats the verb and adds a genuine explanation, which is the move that distinguishes a repair from a retraction: the joke is withdrawn, the observation is kept. «Шутки у тебя так себе» (tak see-BYE), 'so-so', is the offended party's evaluation, and it is mild. «Ну ты чего» then shifts the frame from the joke to the reaction, which is either affectionate or reproachful depending on tone, and in this exchange it is affectionate with an edge. A learner who says «Извини, это была шутка» (eez-vee-NEE, EH-ta BY-la SHOOT-ka) has apologised, which is grammatically fine and socially heavier: it treats the exchange as a conflict rather than as a failed joke.
lessons.question: You tell a colleague «Ну ты и мастер!» after he fixes the printer, intending a sincere compliment, and he answers «Сарказм?» (sar-KAZM), 'sarcasm?'. What went wrong?
lessons.answer: The frame «ну ты и» plus a noun is the standard ironic compliment, especially with a flat or drawn-out delivery, so it was heard as mockery; sincere versions are «Вот это мастер!» (VOT EH-ta MAS-ter) or «Ну ты молодец» (noo ty ma-la-DYETS), with a clear rise and no drawl.
lessons.distractor: Nothing went wrong in the language; «мастер» is a neutral word and the colleague simply has no sense of humour.
lessons.correction: The word is neutral; the frame is not. «Ну ты и...» is a fixed construction for an ironic evaluation, roughly 'you are quite the...', and Russian speakers read it as sarcastic by default unless the intonation is unmistakably warm. The colleague's «Сарказм?» was a request for clarification, not an accusation, and the correct reply is a short sincere recast, «Нет, правда, здорово получилось» (nyet, PRAV-da, ZDA-ro-va pa-loo-CHEE-las), 'no, really, you did it well'. The general lesson is that irony in Russian lives in the frame and the melody rather than in the words, which is why a sincere sentence built on an ironic frame cannot be rescued by good intentions. When in doubt, use a frame with only one reading, such as «вот это» plus a positive noun.

depth.definitions: Irony is the expression of a meaning that contradicts the literal sense, and sarcasm is irony with an intent to wound or mock. A repair is the move that follows a failed speech act and attempts to restore the relationship, which is what «да шучу я» performs. A frame is a fixed construction with slots, such as «ну ты и» plus a noun, whose evaluative direction is set by the construction rather than by the slot filler. A euphemistic expletive is a mild word substituted for a stronger one, which is the status of блин. An anecdote in English is a short account of an incident, while анекдот in Russian is a joke with a punchline, and the false equivalence is a lexical trap rather than a translation problem. Prerequisites: the particles of lesson 102, since же and -то carry the shared assumptions that irony exploits, and the reaction words of lesson 142, since «да ладно» and «ну да» share the disbelief function.
depth.mechanism: The mechanism of irony is a mismatch between what is said and what is meant, and every language needs a way to signal that the mismatch is intended. English uses tone and, in writing, punctuation or an emoji. Russian uses three devices. The first is the frame: «ну ты и», «ну да, конечно» and «ага, сейчас» are constructions that have only an ironic reading, so the speaker can be understood without any special tone. The second is intonation, which in Russian can be extremely marked, a drawl on the stressed syllable or an exaggerated rise, and it is the device that carries the most weight in speech. The third is the particle system, because же and -то present a statement as already shared, and a statement presented as shared when it is obviously false is the definition of irony. The repair system works by a different mechanism, which is frame shifting. «Да шучу я» moves the frame from 'claim' to 'joke', and «ну ты чего» moves it from 'joke' to 'your reaction', and each move changes what the other person is being asked to do. That is why the choice of repair is a choice about the relationship rather than about the content.
depth.secondExample: An ironic exchange at a meeting, where the markers do the work without any explicit signal. «Ну да, конечно, мы всё успеем за неделю». (noo DA, ka-NYESH-na, my VSYO oos-PYE-yem za nee-DYE-lyoo.) 'Yeah, right, of course we will manage everything in a week.' «Ты серьёзно?» (ty see-RYOZ-na?) 'Are you serious?' «Конечно. Как же иначе». (ka-NYESH-na. kak zhe ee-NA-che.) 'Of course. How else.' The first sentence is a double marker: «ну да» plus «конечно», both affirmative, and the combination with a flat delivery is the strongest Russian signal of disbelief. The second speaker's «ты серьёзно» is not a request for information but an invitation to drop the irony, which is the same function as the English 'are you being sarcastic'. The third answer escalates by adding «как же иначе» (kak zhe ee-NA-che), 'how else', with же marking the assumption as shared and therefore absurd. Nobody has said anything negative, and the position is completely clear. A learner who tries to reproduce this with words alone, for example «Я не верю, что мы успеем» (ya ne VYE-roo, shto my oos-PYE-yem), 'I do not believe we will manage', has the same opinion and none of the irony, and in a meeting that is often the better choice, because irony at work depends on a shared history that a learner may not have.
depth.mistake: Four errors recur. The first is translating «ну ты чего» as 'what is wrong with you', which converts an affectionate reproach into an accusation; the phrase has no English equivalent and should be learned as a move rather than as words. The second is using «это шутка» as the standard repair, which labels the joke and thereby admits it failed; «да шучу я» is the idiomatic repair because it withdraws the claim and keeps the observation. The third is missing the false friend анекдот, with the result that a learner asks for an anecdote and receives a joke, or offers a personal story when a joke was requested. The fourth is register: блин and прикол are peer language, and an ironic «ну да, конечно» to a client reads as contempt rather than as humour. A fifth error is prosodic and hard to correct without practice: learners deliver Russian irony with English melody, a light rise at the end, where Russian wants either a flat line or a heavy drawl, and the result is heard as sincerity. Recording yourself and comparing with a native clip is the only reliable fix.
depth.application: Take three jokes or ironic remarks you would make in your own language and write each one in Russian twice: once with an explicit marker, «шучу» or «ну да, конечно», and once with no marker at all, relying on the frame and the wording. Read both aloud and decide which one you could actually deliver without the tone that makes it work. Then write the repair for each, choosing between «да шучу я», «ну ты чего» and a plain apology, and say in English what relationship each repair assumes. Next, find a five-minute clip of a Russian comedian or interviewer and transcribe only the moments where the audience laughs; mark what preceded each laugh, a frame, a particle or a pause. The pattern is usually a frame plus a pause, and seeing it in someone else's speech is more convincing than any rule. The task takes forty minutes and produces a small inventory of frames you can use with confidence.
depth.summary: Russian humour is managed by repairs and frames. шутка labels a joke and admits it has failed, «да шучу я» withdraws the claim while keeping the observation, and «ну ты чего» shifts the frame to the other person's reaction with a mixture of reproach and affection that English cannot reproduce in one phrase. Irony is carried by frames such as «ну ты и», «ну да, конечно» and «ага, сейчас», by heavy intonation and by the particles же and -то, which present a claim as shared and therefore as obviously false. анекдот means joke, not anecdote. The safest strategy for a learner is to use frames with a single reading, to repair with «да шучу я» rather than with a label, and to keep блин, прикол and «ну да, конечно» away from clients.

readings.title: Википедия, «Ирония»
readings.note: Read the lead and the section on irony as a trope. The article defines irony as a statement whose meaning contradicts its form and distinguishes it from related figures, which is the conceptual basis for the frame analysis in this lesson. lessons.title: Switching ты and вы inside a conversation: the pronouns, who may propose the change, and when the shift is an insult
lessons.explanation: The choice between ты (ty) and вы (vy) is the most consequential grammatical decision in Russian social life, and it is usually taught as a fact about strangers and friends. The interesting part is what happens when the choice changes mid-conversation, because Russian treats the pronouns as a running measurement of the relationship rather than as a fixed label. The basics first. ты is the singular familiar pronoun; вы is both the plural and the singular polite pronoun, and the two functions are distinguished by context rather than by form. Agreement follows the pronoun and not the person: «ты сказал» (ty ska-ZAL) against «вы сказали» (vy ska-ZA-lee), «ты готов» (ty ga-TOF) against «вы готовы» (vy ga-TO-vy), «твой» (tvoy) against «ваш» (vash). In writing, Вы is sometimes capitalised in a personal letter to a single addressee as a mark of particular respect, a convention inherited from nineteenth century letter writing; modern style guides disagree about it, emails overwhelmingly use lowercase вы, and a learner is safe with lowercase everywhere except a formal congratulation. The defaults are learnable. Family and close friends take ты from the first word. Children take ты from adults, always, and a child who says вы to a parent is joking or quoting. University teachers take вы plus the first name and patronymic, «Иван Петрович» (ee-VAN pee-TRO-veech), and so do officials, doctors, clients and anyone whose surname you do not know. Students among themselves take ты almost immediately. The workplace is the variable zone: a small team may be on ты within a week, a bank will be on вы for years, and the deciding factors are age, rank and the local culture of the office rather than any rule. What matters for a learner is that the pronoun is only one third of the package. The other two thirds are the name form and the verb agreement, and they move together. ты pairs with the bare first name, often a diminutive, «Саша» (SA-sha) or «Саш» (SASH) in direct address. вы pairs with the first name plus patronymic, or with the surname and a title. «Ты, Иван Петрович» mixes the two and is the single most recognisable learner error in this area, because it grants intimacy with the pronoun and withholds it with the name. The change itself is where the social grammar lives. A switch from вы to ты is an offer of closeness, and it is offered rather than taken: the older, senior or more established party proposes, and the other accepts. The formulae are «Давай на ты» (da-VAY na TY), 'let's use ты', «Перейдём на ты?» (pee-ree-DYOM na TY), 'shall we move to ты', and the more cautious «Можно на ты?» (MOZH-na na TY), 'may we use ты'. Acceptance is «Давай» or «Хорошо» (ha-ra-SHO), 'fine'. Refusal is rare and is delivered as a postponement, «Давайте пока на вы» (da-VAY-tye pa-KA na VY), 'let's stay on вы for now', which is a complete answer and should not be pressed. The reverse switch is the one that does damage. In a relationship that has settled on ты, a return to вы is a withdrawal of closeness, and because it is a withdrawal it is read as a sanction. The sentence «Вы мне это обещали» (vy mnye EH-ta a-bee-SHCHAL-ee), 'you promised me this', said by a manager who has been using ты, is not more polite than the ты version; it is colder, and the explicit pronoun makes the coldness deliberate. The most explicit form of the sanction is a metalinguistic statement, «Мы с вами на вы» (my s VA-mee na VY), 'you and I are on вы', or the sharper «Я вам не ты» (ya vam ne TY), 'I am not ты to you', which a person says when someone has taken a familiarity that was not offered. Russian literature has a famous treatment of the opposite direction. Pushkin's short poem «Ты и вы» (TY ee VY) describes a slip in which a woman, speaking to a man she loves, replaces the formal вы with the intimate ты by accident: «Пустое вы сердечным ты / Она, обмолвясь, заменила» (POOS-ta-ye VY ser-DYECH-nym TY / a-NA ab-MOL-vyas za-mee-NEE-la), 'the empty вы she replaced, slipping, with a heartfelt ты'. The poem is the best evidence that the pronouns are not decoration: a single slip is enough to reveal a feeling, and the man in the poem is transformed by it.
lessons.example: A first meeting at work, then a shift two months later. «Здравствуйте, вы новый аналитик?» (zdra-stvooy-tye, vy NO-vy a-na-LEE-teek?) 'Hello, are you the new analyst?' «Да, меня зовут Анна». (da, mee-NYA za-VOOt A-na.) 'Yes, my name is Anna.' «Очень приятно. Иван Петрович». (O-chen pree-YAT-na. ee-VAN pee-TRO-veech.) 'Pleased to meet you. Ivan Petrovich.' «Очень приятно. Вы давно здесь работаете?» (O-chen pree-YAT-na. vy dav-NO zdyes ra-BO-ta-ee-tye?) 'Pleased to meet you. Have you worked here long?' Two months later, the same two people. «Анна, давай на ты?» (A-na, da-VAY na TY?) 'Listen, Anna, shall we use ты?' «Давай. Только на работе всё равно иногда сбиваюсь». (da-VAY. TOL-ka na ra-BO-tye vsyo rav-NO ee-na-GDA s-bee-VA-yus.) 'Let's. Only at work I still slip sometimes.' «Ничего, я тоже». (nee-chee-VO, ya TO-zhe.) 'No problem, me too.' Now the sanction, six months later, after a broken promise. «Иван Петрович, вы мне это обещали». (ee-VAN pee-TRO-veech, vy mnye EH-ta a-bee-SHCHAL-ee.) 'Ivan Petrovich, you promised me this.' The three excerpts are one relationship in three states. In the first, вы plus имя-отчество is the complete package, and the reciprocal question uses the вы form of the verb, работаете. In the second, the proposal comes from the senior party, is phrased as a question and is accepted with давай; the note about slipping is realistic, because the switch is a habit that takes weeks. In the third, the return to вы plus the patronymic is the same package in reverse, and the pronoun is explicit, which is the signal. Note that nothing in the third sentence is grammatically unusual; the offence is entirely in the choice of address.
lessons.question: A twenty-five-year-old intern wants to be friendly with the sixty-year-old head of department and says «Давай на ты». What has she done, and what should she do instead?
lessons.answer: She has taken a familiarity that only the senior party can offer, which puts the head of department in the position of having to refuse her in public; she should stay on вы with the first name and patronymic until he proposes the change, and if he does, accept with «Давай» or «Хорошо».
lessons.distractor: Nothing is wrong, because ты is the friendly form and a young colleague should show that she is approachable.
lessons.correction: The T-V system is asymmetric: the senior party proposes and the junior accepts, so the same sentence that is warm from the head of department to the intern is presumptuous in the other direction. The intern has not been rude in her intention and she has been rude in her effect, because she has forced a decision that etiquette says is his. The repair is not an apology but a return to the вы package, «Извините, я по привычке» (eez-vee-NEE-tye, ya pa pree-VYCH-kye), 'sorry, force of habit', and then вы with the patronymic. If the relationship develops, the invitation will come, and it will usually be phrased as «Давай на ты» or «Перейдём на ты». A learner's rule is simple: mirror the other person's pronoun and name form until invited, and treat an invitation as something to accept rather than to initiate.

depth.definitions: T-V distinction is the linguistic term for the two-pronoun system, named after the Latin tu and vos, in which one form marks familiarity or solidarity and the other marks distance or respect. Power is the dimension that gives one speaker the right to initiate a change, and solidarity is the dimension that makes the change desirable. A register package is the set of choices that move together, here the pronoun, the verb agreement and the name form. A metalinguistic move is a statement about the language itself, such as «Мы с вами на вы», used to renegotiate the relationship explicitly. A diminutive is an affectionate or familiar form of a name, such as Саша from Александр, and it belongs to the ты package. Prerequisites: the pronoun declension of lesson 6, the short adjectives of lesson 5, and the hedging and politeness material of lesson 77, which introduced the pronouns in their written registers.
depth.mechanism: The pronouns work as an index rather than a description: they do not say anything about the relationship, they enact it. That is why a change of pronoun changes the relationship without any other word changing, and why the change is felt as an event rather than as a correction. The asymmetry comes from power: the person with more of it can offer closeness without risk, because a refusal costs the other party more than it costs him. The solidarity dimension explains the direction of travel in modern Russian, which is towards ты in more contexts than fifty years ago, especially among the young and online, and towards вы in customer service, where distance protects both sides. The three-part package is what makes the system learnable: pronoun, agreement and name form must move together, and a mismatch is read as either ignorance or a deliberate signal. That is also why the return from ты to вы is so legible: it is the same package moving backwards, and everyone in the room can see it.
depth.secondExample: A customer service exchange, where the вы package is doing professional work. «Добрый день. Подскажите, пожалуйста, вы оформляли заказ на прошлой неделе?» (DOB-ry dyen. pat-SKA-zhee-tye, pa-ZHA-las-ta, vy a-form-LYA-lee za-KAZ na PROSH-lay nee-DYE-le?) 'Good afternoon. Could you tell me, did you place an order last week?' «Да, но я не получила подтверждение». (da, no ya ne pa-loo-CHEE-la pat-tverzh-DYE-nee-ye.) 'Yes, but I did not receive a confirmation.' «Сейчас посмотрю. Вы не могли бы назвать номер заказа?» (see-CHAS pa-smat-RYOO. vy ne mag-LEE by naz-VAT NO-mer za-KA-za?) 'Let me check. Could you give me the order number?' «Конечно. И ещё: вы можете писать мне на почту». (ka-NYESH-na. ee yeshchyo: vy MO-zhe-tye pee-SAT mnye na POCH-too.) 'Of course. And also: you can write to me by email.' Every verb is plural, every request is framed as a negative question or with пожалуйста, and the customer responds in the same package, which is the reciprocity that makes the exchange smooth. Now imagine the same exchange with ты: «Слушай, ты оформляла заказ?» The words would be shorter and the transaction would be faster, and it would be wrong, not because the shop assistant is being friendly but because she has decided on a relationship the customer has not agreed to. That is the practical version of the whole lesson: вы is not colder in customer service, it is the package that keeps both parties from having to negotiate a relationship while buying a phone.
depth.mistake: Four errors recur. The first is the mixed package, «ты, Иван Петрович», which is the most visible learner error and is corrected by matching the name to the pronoun. The second is initiating the switch downwards, as in the question, which is presumptuous even when the intention is warm. The third is failing to notice the sanction when a Russian speaker returns to вы, and answering in ты, which reads as refusing to acknowledge the withdrawal. The fourth is the written convention: learners capitalise Вы in every email, which looks old-fashioned or ironic, or they use ты in a first email to a stranger, which is worse. Diagnostic for all four: identify the pronoun, the verb ending and the name form, and check that the three match and that the most senior person in the exchange used them first. A fifth error is specific to learners whose languages have a T-V system, such as French or Spanish: they assume the Russian thresholds match theirs, and they are usually too quick with ты in shops and too slow with ты among students.
depth.application: Write three short dialogues, each of four turns, in which the same two people meet at three stages: a first meeting at work, a switch proposed and accepted, and a conflict in which one of them returns to вы. Use only the pronoun, the verb agreement and the name form to signal the stage, and give no stage directions. Then read the third dialogue aloud and check whether the return to вы is audible without any explanation; if it is not, the package is not consistent. Next, write an email to a Russian-speaking stranger asking for information, and decide consciously between вы and Вы, and between «Здравствуйте» (zdra-stvooy-tye) and «Добрый день» (DOB-ry dyen). Finally, note the pronouns you actually use with three Russian-speaking contacts and compare them with what you think the relationship is. The gap between the two lists is your real lesson.
depth.summary: ты and вы are not simply familiar and polite; they are an index of the relationship, and a change of pronoun changes the relationship. The package has three parts, pronoun, verb agreement and name form, and they must match: ты with the bare name, вы with the name and patronymic. The senior or older party offers the switch with «Давай на ты» or «Перейдём на ты», the other accepts or postpones, and a junior who initiates is presumptuous rather than friendly. Returning from ты to вы is a withdrawal of closeness and is read as a sanction, which is why «Вы мне это обещали» from a manager who has been on ты is colder than the ты version. Pushkin's «Ты и вы» is the classic demonstration that a single slip of the pronoun can carry a whole feeling.

lessons.title: Capstone: a fast exchange, move by move, and the reply you owe each move
lessons.explanation: This lesson assembles the unit into one exchange of thirteen turns and then slows it down. The exchange is a telephone call between two friends in their thirties, one of whom has two tickets for a Saturday exhibition. Read it once at speed, then read the analysis, then answer the five replies yourself before looking at the models. «Алло?» (al-LO?) 'Hello?' «Привет, это я. Удобно?» (pree-VYET, EH-ta ya. oo-DOB-na?) 'Hi, it is me. Is now convenient?' «Да, нормально. Что нового?» (da, nar-MAL-na. shto NO-va-va?) 'Yes, fine. What is new?' «Слушай, какие планы на субботу?» (SLOO-shay, ka-KEE-ye PLA-ny na soo-BO-too?) 'Listen, what are your plans for Saturday?' «Да ничего особенного. А что?» (da nee-chee-VO a-SO-ben-na-va. a SHTO?) 'Nothing special. Why?' «У меня два билета на выставку. Пойдём?» (oo mee-NYA dva bee-LYE-ta na VY-staf-koo. pay-DYOM?) 'I have two tickets for the exhibition. Shall we go?' «Ого, ничего себе. А во сколько?» (a-GO, nee-chee-VO see-BYEH. a va SKOL-ka?) 'Wow. At what time?' «В семь. Только, в общем, есть один момент». (f syem. TOL-ka, VOP-shem, yest a-DEEN ma-MENT.) 'At seven. Only, well, there is one thing.' «Ну не знаю, я до шести работаю». (noo ne ZNA-yoo, ya da shee-TEE ra-BO-ta-yoo.) 'Well, I don't know, I work until six.' «Успеешь. От метро двадцать минут». (oos-PYE-yesh. at meet-RO DVA-tsat mee-NOOT.) 'You will make it. It is twenty minutes from the metro.' «Ладно, давай. Только если опоздаю, не обижайся». (LAD-na, da-VAY. TOL-ka YES-lee a-paz-DA-yoo, ne a-bee-ZHAY-sya.) 'All right, let's. Only if I am late, don't be offended.' «Да шучу я, ты никогда не опаздываешь. Значит, в семь у входа. Договорились?» (da shoo-CHOO ya. ZNA-cheet, f syem oo FHO-da. da-ga-va-REE-lees?) 'I'm joking. So, at seven at the entrance. Agreed?' «Договорились. До связи». (da-ga-va-REE-lees. da SVYA-zee.) 'Agreed. Until we are in touch.' The turns are not a conversation in the sense of free talk; they are a fixed sequence of moves, and every move has a small set of acceptable realisations. Turn one is a channel test, and it is answered by turn two with identification plus a permission request, «удобно», which is the Russian way of asking whether the next minute belongs to the caller. Turn three answers the permission and opens the topic with «что нового», a news invitation. Turn four is the availability question, and it is answered in turn five with «ничего особенного» plus «а что», which is the shortest way to say 'tell me what you actually want', because the speaker wants the plan before she evaluates it. Turn six is the proposal, using пойдём without давай because пойти is a verb of motion. Turn seven is a reaction plus a request for detail, «а во сколько», and the reaction «ого, ничего себе» is stacked, which is normal and marks genuine surprise. Turn eight contains the complication marker, «только» (TOL-ka), 'only', plus «в общем» and «есть один момент» (yest a-DEEN ma-MENT), 'there is one thing', which is how a Russian speaker announces bad news without delivering it yet. Turn nine is the hedge, «ну не знаю», followed by the reason, which is the pattern of lesson 143. Turn ten answers the doubt with a calculation rather than a reassurance, which is the Russian preference: facts instead of comfort. Turn eleven is the acceptance with a condition, «ладно, давай» plus «только если», and the condition is a face-saving pre-apology for lateness. Turn twelve defuses the condition with «да шучу я» and a joke about her punctuality, then closes with «значит» plus the details plus «договорились», which is the confirmation formula from lesson 145. Turn thirteen confirms and signs off with «до связи». Thirteen turns, each one a recognisable move, and the whole thing takes forty seconds. The point of the capstone is not to memorise the script; it is to recognise the move before you have to answer it, because the answer is determined by the move and not by the topic.
lessons.example: The same moves in a different key, at work and on вы. «Добрый день, Ирина Петровна. Удобно говорить?» (DOB-ry dyen, ee-REE-na peet-ROV-na. oo-DOB-na ga-va-REET?) 'Good afternoon, Irina Petrovna. Is it convenient to talk?' «Да, конечно. Что случилось?» (da, ka-NYESH-na. shto sloo-CHEE-las?) 'Yes, of course. What has happened?' «Хотел уточнить по поводу встречи в четверг». (ha-TYEL oo-tach-NEET pa PO-va-doo FSTRYE-chee f cheet-VYERK.) 'I wanted to check about the meeting on Thursday.' «Слушаю вас». (SLOO-sha-yoo vas.) 'I am listening.' «Вы сможете в четыре?» (vy SMO-zhe-tye f chee-TY-re?) 'Will you be able at four?' «В четыре у меня комиссия. Давайте в пять». (f chee-TY-re oo mee-NYA ka-MEE-see-ya. da-VAY-tye f pyat.) 'At four I have a committee. Let us say five.' «Хорошо, в пять. Я вас жду». (ha-ra-SHO, f pyat. ya vas zhdoo.) 'Fine, at five. I will be expecting you.' The same moves appear in a different register, and the differences are systematic rather than decorative. The greeting is a time-of-day formula plus the name and patronymic, not привет. The permission request uses the infinitive «удобно говорить» rather than the short adjective «удобно», which is the written-leaning variant. The proposal is not an invitation but a request to confirm, «хотел уточнить» (ha-TYEL oo-tach-NEET), 'I wanted to check', which is the standard way to open a work call without sounding like a demand. The complication is delivered as a competing commitment rather than as a doubt, «у меня комиссия», because at work a fact does more work than a hedge. The alternative is offered with «давайте», the plural imperative, not «давай». And the close is a statement of expectation, «я вас жду», rather than «до связи», because the meeting is fixed. Learn the moves and both registers become available; learn only the phrases and you will be fluent in one room and lost in the next.
lessons.question: In the capstone call, turn eight says «В семь. Только, в общем, есть один момент». You are free at seven but the phrase makes you cautious. Which reply is best, and why?
lessons.answer: «А какой момент?» (a ka-KOY ma-MENT?), 'what kind of thing', asks for the complication before you commit, which is what the marker «только» invites; a close second is «Ну не знаю, что там?» if you want to keep the hedge, but the direct request is cleaner.
lessons.distractor: «Ладно, давай» (LAD-na, da-VAY), 'all right, let's', because accepting quickly shows enthusiasm and the other person will explain later.
lessons.correction: «Только» announces a complication and «есть один момент» withholds it, which is a bid for your attention rather than a complete statement. Accepting before hearing it gives away your only chance to negotiate, and the other person will then have to raise the problem after you have agreed, which is more awkward for both of you. The move that fits is a request for the missing information, and «а какой момент» is the shortest natural form. The distractor is not rude; it is simply one move too early. In the dialogue the same slot is filled by «ну не знаю» plus a reason, which is the softer version and works because the speaker already knows the complication involves her working hours.

depth.definitions: A move is a functional step in an exchange, such as a proposal, a hedge or a confirmation, and it is realised by phrases rather than by a single phrase. A adjacency pair is a pair of turns in which the first makes the second relevant, for example a proposal and a verdict. A pre-sequence is a move that prepares the ground for the main move, such as «удобно?» before the topic or «только» before the complication. A register package, as in lesson 149, is the set of choices that move together, here greeting, pronoun, name form and closing. A capstone is a task that requires the integration of previously separate skills under time pressure. Prerequisites: every lesson in this unit, plus the aspect system and the motion verbs that make пойдём and успеешь work, and the case system that makes «на субботу», «до шести» and «у входа» correct.
depth.mechanism: The exchange is fast because the moves are predictable, and predictability is what buys speed. Each turn narrows the set of relevant next turns, so neither speaker has to plan the whole conversation; the first turn opens the channel, the permission request authorises the topic, the news question hands over the floor, and the proposal creates a slot that can only be filled by a verdict or a request for detail. The markers do the same work at a smaller scale: «только» warns that the next clause will complicate something, «в общем» says that the speaker is coming to the point, «значит» says that a conclusion is being drawn. A learner who can hear the warning markers can prepare a reply while the other person is still speaking, which is what conversational speed actually is. The capstone also demonstrates the division between content and move: the tickets, the exhibition and the hour are arbitrary, while the sequence of moves would survive any substitution. That is why the analysis is more useful than the script.
depth.secondExample: The same moves when the plan collapses, which is the version a learner is most likely to face. «Слушай, в субботу не получится». (SLOO-shay, f soo-BO-too ne pa-LOO-cheet-sya.) 'Listen, Saturday will not work out.' «Да ладно! Почему?» (da LAD-na! pa-chee-MOO?) 'No way! Why?' «Заболел коллега, я работаю». (za-ba-LYEL ka-LEE-ga, ya ra-BO-ta-yoo.) 'A colleague is ill, I am working.' «Ну ты чего, мы же договаривались». (noo ty chee-VO, my zhe da-ga-VA-ree-va-lees.) 'Come on, we agreed.' «Извини. Давай в воскресенье?» (eez-vee-NEE. da-VAY v vas-kree-SYE-nee-ye?) 'Sorry. Shall we do Sunday?' «Ладно, давай. Только не утром». (LAD-na, da-VAY. TOL-ka ne OOT-ram.) 'All right, let's. Only not in the morning.' «Договорились. В час дня». (da-ga-va-REE-lees. f chas dnya.) 'Agreed. At one in the afternoon.' The collapse keeps the shape. The news arrives with «не получится», the reaction is «да ладно» plus a request for the reason, the reason is a fact, the reproach is «ну ты чего» plus «мы же договаривались» with же marking the shared commitment, the repair is an apology plus an alternative, and the renegotiation closes with the confirmation. Note that the reproach is mild and that it is answered, not deflected: «извини» acknowledges it, and the alternative moves the conversation forward. A learner who skips the acknowledgement and goes straight to the new proposal sounds as if the commitment did not matter.
depth.mistake: Four errors recur in capstone performance. The first is answering a move with the wrong move, usually by giving a verdict before hearing the proposal, as in the question above. Diagnostic: label the other person's last turn before you speak; if the label is 'proposal', your reply must be a verdict or a request for detail, not a new topic. The second is answering a hedge as if it were a refusal, so that «ну не знаю» gets a defence instead of more information. The third is register leakage, which in this exchange means using давай, я пас and привет in the work version or «хотел уточнить» with a friend, where it sounds stiff. The fourth is failing to close: learners often end a successful arrangement without «договорились» or «записал», and the plan is then remembered by nobody. Diagnostic: if the last three turns contain no confirmation word, the arrangement is not finished. A fifth error is prosodic, and it is the hardest to fix: speaking every turn with the same melody, which makes a reaction sound like a statement and a joke sound like an insult.
depth.application: Perform the capstone aloud, taking both parts, then perform it again answering only the five slots marked below with your own words: after «что нового», after «пойдём», after «есть один момент», after «успеешь», and after «договорились». Record the second performance and listen for three things: whether your reactions come before your questions, whether your hedges carry a reason, and whether your closing contains a confirmation. Then change one variable and redo the exchange: make the two speakers colleagues on вы, or make the plan collapse, or make one of them refuse. Each variation should take two minutes and should require no new vocabulary, only the same moves in a different key. Finally, write the exchange out from memory in thirteen lines and compare it with the version in this lesson; the differences will show you which moves you have actually internalised and which you are still translating. The whole task takes forty minutes and is the assessment for the unit.
depth.summary: A fast exchange is a predictable sequence of moves: channel test, identification and permission, news invitation, availability question, proposal, reaction and request for detail, complication marker, hedge with a reason, verdict with a condition, repair and confirmation, and a channel-specific farewell. The phrases are replaceable and the order is not, which is why hearing the move is more valuable than memorising the script. Markers such as только, в общем and значит warn you what is coming while the other person is still speaking, and that warning is what conversational speed consists of. The same moves run in a formal register with вы, имя-отчество and «давайте», and in a collapse with «не получится», «ну ты чего» and an alternative. Close every arrangement with «договорились», and answer a complication before you accept.

readings.title: Cornell, Beginning Russian Grammar: 'Deverbals: written vs. conversational style'
readings.note: Read the whole page, which is one short summary. It states the contrast this capstone depends on, that participles and deverbal nouns belong to written style while который clauses belong to conversation, and it points to the pages that treat each form. It is the grammatical version of the register difference the two dialogues demonstrate. Caveat: the page is a summary with a legacy Cyrillic encoding, so read the English and take the forms from the earlier lessons.

readings.title: Wikipedia, 'Register (sociolinguistics)'
readings.note: Read the lead and the section on register as a functional variety. The article supplies the concept used in the second dialogue, that the same moves can be performed in a different key with systematic changes in vocabulary and grammar rather than with decoration. Caveat: it is a theory article with English examples and no Russian data, and the term is used in several competing senses, so read the lead carefully.

readings.title: Википедия, «Речевой акт»

It is the frame for treating each turn as a move, and for the claim that «договорились» is a commitment rather than a comment. Caveat: the article is a philosophy of language summary with examples from the classic literature, not a description of Russian conversation.

Caveat: this is a live news feed, so the specific stories change daily and the page is not an archive; read it for the register, not for content.

visual.title: Thirteen-turn exchange map with its moves and five reply slots
visual.description: A labelled two-column map of the capstone call with the turn number, the speaker, the move and the Russian frame, plus five marked slots where the learner must produce a reply. Rendered as text steps, not as an image.
steps: Step 1, draw a two-column table with thirteen rows, one per turn, and label the columns 'turn' and 'move'. Write the move names in order down the second column: channel test, identification, permission, news invitation, availability, proposal, reaction, complication, hedge, calculation, verdict, confirmation, farewell.

Step 2, fill the frames. Put the Russian phrase for each move beside its name, from «Алло» to «До связи», and draw an arrow from each frame to the next to show that a move makes the next one relevant.

Step 3, mark the five reply slots. Circle the turns after «что нового», «пойдём», «есть один момент», «успеешь» and «договорились», and write beside each circle the kind of reply the slot accepts: a short news item, a reaction plus a question, a request for the complication, a condition, and a confirmation.

Step 4, add the marker row. Under the turns that contain только, в общем, значит and да шучу я, write in the margin what each marker warns the hearer about, because the warning is what allows a reply to be prepared in advance.

Step 5, add the register twin. Draw a second table beside the first with the same moves in the formal key, using «Добрый день», «удобно говорить», «хотел уточнить», «давайте» and «я вас жду», so the moves and the register are visibly separate layers.
